## Virtual math manipulatives: Oomba chat (22 Nov 2026)

The owner: "what happens if the teacher wants to make adjustments with the AI? I am thinking we need to make this an
interactive chat. So if you press draft with AI the Oomba Builder pops up on the right side of the screen and you can
tell it what you'd like it to do. Oomba should know exactly what page you are on for this. For mobile, we could allow
users to minimize the chat and an oomba chat logo would go to the bottom right of the screen."

- **The panel** (public/js/manip-chat.js, public/css/manip-chat.css). "Draft with AI" in the board's tools, and a new
  Oomba button by the board's title, open Oomba's chat. Laptops and tablets (900 px and wider): a panel docked on the
  right below the top bar (380 px, 340 px under 1100 px); the page narrows beside it and the board fits again, nothing
  is covered. Phones: a sheet above the tab bar with Minimize and Close; minimized it is a round Oomba bubble (the logo
  mark) at the bottom right just above the tab bar, with a green dot and "a new answer" in its name when Oomba answered
  meanwhile. Escape in the chat minimizes; focus goes to the composer on open, to the bubble on minimize, back to the
  button that opened it on close. Closing while Oomba is answering minimizes instead, so the answer has a place to land.
  The Builder chat's look: the teacher's words in Mint on the end side, Oomba's on a card with its mark, the same
  composer and Send. Logical properties (RTL), the site's tokens (dark mode), 13 locales (js.manip-chat).
- **The first message is the brief.** On an empty board Oomba says "Tell me the lesson you'd like on this Clock board"
  and offers up to three of the tool's library tasks as chips; on a board with things on it, three ideas (two more
  problems, easier, clearer steps). The grade (Any, K to 8) sits under the composer and goes with every message. The
  old drafter form is no longer opened from the page; draft jobs already running (services/manip-drafts.js) still show
  their progress, notice and fallback as before, and POST /api/manipulatives/draft stays.
- **What Oomba knows (built on the server, services/manip-chat.js).** Each message carries the teacher's own board;
  the server cleans it (cleanState) and builds the context itself: the tool and its grades, whether it is a new board or
  one saved in My boards, whether the teacher is running a live room with this tool, the grade, the title and steps,
  and the items in the practice-set form (each drafted cell's settings in PRACTICE_HELP's words, its box and its answer
  key; a board made by hand as a "free" list of object kinds, numbers and piece counts). Never sticky notes, pen marks,
  text typed on the board, typed answers, labels, students' names or work. A title or step that fails the word rules or
  names one of the teacher's students is left out. The teacher's message passes textProblem and namesIn like a draft
  brief; a message that fails is refused before anything is stored or sent, and the words stay in the box with the
  reason.
- **What Oomba can do.** The model answers plain JSON (no strict json_schema: it hung in production) shaped
  { reply, action: null | { op: "replace", draft: { title, steps, items } } }. A change is always the whole new board,
  run through sanitizeDraft and buildPractice exactly like Draft with AI, then cleanState: every board the chat makes is
  checked and laid out by the code. If every item it sent fails the checks, the board stays and the reply says so. Any
  other action is ignored (a reply only). The page puts a change on the board as one change: the board's own Undo, and
  "Undo Oomba's change" (then "Put it back") under the reply, which also brings back the title and steps. A change that
  arrived while the page was closed is offered once as "Put it on my board".
- **A turn is a job** (like the drafts): POST /api/manipulatives/chat checks, stores the message and returns; the answer
  is made in this process, apart from any request, and the page asks every 2 s while it waits ("Oomba is thinking 0:12",
  "You can close this page. The answer will wait here."). A refresh shows the same wait and applies the answer when it
  comes. One turn at a time per board (409 chatBusy). One AI call per turn with the one 90 s budget (services/ai-call.js
  callAi), the AI budget pool ('free', recordUsage), config.builderModel, max_tokens 3000, effort low; every failure is
  one warn line without the teacher's words and a calm answer ("Oomba couldn't answer this time; your board is
  unchanged", and its timeout, busy, resting and restart sentences) with Try again (the failed pair makes way for the
  same words sent again) and Edit (the words back in the box). A turn cut off by a restart ends as failed ('restart')
  the next time the chat is read. Rate limit: the drafts' own bucket (manip-ai, 30 an hour, shared with Draft with AI).
- **Kept** (migration 0103_manipulatives_chat, manip_chats): one conversation per teacher and board (a recent board's id,
  or new:<tool> until the board's first autosave, which then takes it over within 30 minutes; an older new-board chat
  is dropped when a new board opens). The newest 20 turns; 8 go to the AI with a message; the built board's state only
  on the newest 3 changes. Messages at most 1000 characters, replies 600, board context 8000. Deleted with the board
  (deleteBoard, and recent boards trimmed or expired: pruned on the next read), after 60 days untouched, and with the
  account (forgetUser and the users foreign key).
- **Endpoints** (hosts only, behind the Teacher plan gate; students, kids and guests get the 404, staff without the plan
  403 teacherPlan): GET /api/manipulatives/chat?tool=&boardId= (the conversation: turns, the pending turn, the grade),
  POST /api/manipulatives/chat ({ tool, boardId?, title, text, grade?, state, retry? }: -> the conversation), POST
  /api/manipulatives/chat/applied ({ tool, boardId?, turnId }: the change was put on the board, not offered again).
- **Judgment calls.** Only "replace" (the whole board) is implemented: an "edit" with a list of changes would need its
  own checks and the whole-board draft already goes through the tested ones. The chat is on the teacher's own board, where
  Draft with AI lives; the live room's teacher view has no Oomba button yet (its context knows when a room runs on the
  same tool). The board's own Undo brings back the pieces and objects; "Undo Oomba's change" brings back the title and
  steps too. Oomba replies in the teacher's language; what goes on the board stays US English for children, as drafts.
- **Tests:** manip-chat (a reply-only turn and what the AI sees; a change built by the code, offered once, the history
  on the next turn; bad JSON and a timeout with Try again; names, personal details and short messages refused before
  the AI; students, guests and a free teacher refused; one turn at a time; a restart; the chat following its board and
  going with it and the account; the context and the answer reader) and manip-chat-browser (Chromium: docked on a
  laptop with the board beside it, a change and both Undos; a refresh mid-answer, a failed answer and Try again, a
  refused message keeping its words; an iPhone 13 sheet above the tab bar, the bubble with its dot, reopened, Escape).
  manip-saving-browser starts its draft jobs through the API now.

Two owner asks. "When you place down a chart, table, or graph, it should always be locked in place by default." And,
looking at the 📋 Steps editor: "where are the steps laid out for the students? I see them written here, but how would
a student see it? I am thinking we need to put the steps on the actual board."

  work mat, the five-frame, ten-frame and double ten-frame, the part-part-whole mat, the hundred board, the coordinate
  grid, the number line and the bar model. A new one starts with the wheel's ordinary lock (`locked: true`, no author)
  wherever it is placed: the palette, a new board's first object, an AI draft (`draftLayout`), a practice set

  first-format boards migrate unlocked). The room's rule is unchanged: a student's own locks (theirs, or a chart in a

- **The steps card** (`manip-room.js` `stepCardHtml`, one design with the live square's strip: its tint, 📌 and words).
  Pinned above the board and joined to its top edge, so nothing on the board is ever under it (it is not a piece and

  chips like the board's zoom buttons (the viewer moves through their own board's steps) and a quiet ✕ for the

- **Where steps show.** The teacher's own board and any board opened from a share code or a saved board: the card.
  A live session (a session started from a board, or a pushed board's steps as the deck): unchanged, the strip in
  every square and the big step in the teacher's area, still never a future step sent to a student. The session PDF
  now starts with the session's steps, numbered. Students do not open boards outside a session (Teacher plan gate), so
  the room's strip is their view; the room's teacher area is also the projection view.
- **Tests:** `manip-board.test.js` (every placement path locks a backdrop, others and old boards stay as they were),
  `manipulatives.test.js` (the PDF's Steps block), `manip-steps-browser.test.js` (iPhone 13 and laptop: the card above

## Mistake Hunt: proofreading passages, Phase 1 (22 Nov 2026)
Owner, on the plan and mockup (a proofreading game in the spirit of passageproof.com, played end to end first): "This is
brilliant. Go ahead and build", and that a printable worksheet matters (a student sheet with write-on space, Name and
Date, a small proofreading-marks legend, "find N mistakes", and a separate staff-only answer key, US Letter, black on
white). **Owner decisions, taken with the plan's recommendations:**
- **Name:** "Mistake Hunt" is a working name; a **trademark check is still pending** (as for Doodle Hoot).
- **Entirely our own:** original name, look, code, mistake rules, word lists and passages. Nothing from the source
  site (its name, branding, text, code or word lists) is used; we did not ask teacher.dev to reuse anything.
- **Free like Crossword:** the game, saving, My worksheets, print, the key and Assign are free; the AI tools come in
  Phase 2 (and the costliest ones may go behind the Teacher plan then: still the owner's call).
- **English passages in v1**, the page in all 13 site languages (passages, wrong words and the rules stay US English).
- **Students see a hint while playing**, with fixed why lines we wrote for each kind of mistake (no AI in Phase 1).

**What it is.** `seed-games/mistake-hunt.html`, an official Learn game (words, grades 1-8; migration
`0104_mistake_hunt_shelf`), hand-written like Crossword, outside the Oomba Kit, in the mockup's look (cream cards, Leaf
and Spark, Bricolage Grotesque, light and dark). A teacher's **passage set** is 1 to 8 passages; each is the teacher's
correct text with mistakes planted in it by code, never by AI, so the key is always the teacher's own text.
- **The planter and checker** (`proof-core`, the pure block between `proof-core:begin` and `proof-core:end`; the server
  runs the same block from the same file through `server/services/proof-core.js`): text in tokens (a word with its
  punctuation); a mistake is a token range `[a, b)` and the wrong words students see there. **30 kinds in 5 groups**, each
  with a Common Core Language code (all real codes in `server/standards/ccss-ela.json`) and a why line:
  - Spelling: commonly misspelled word (L.4.2d), doubled or dropped letter (L.3.2e), spelling with an ending (L.3.2e),
    ie or ei (L.3.2f);
  - Word choice: there/their/they're, to/too/two, its/it's, your/you're, sound-alike words, mixed-up words (then/than,
    affect/effect, a lot/alot; all L.4.1g), could of (L.6.1e, off by default);
  - Grammar: subject and verb (L.3.1f), irregular past (L.2.1d), verb tense shift (L.5.1d), pronoun case (L.6.1a),
    adjective or adverb (L.2.1e), irregular plural (L.2.1b);
  - Sentences: run-on, comma splice, fragment (L.4.1f);
  - Capitals and punctuation: end punctuation (L.1.2b), capital at the start and capital I (L.K.2a), names and places
    (L.2.2a), stray capital (L.4.2a, off by default), possessive and contraction apostrophes (L.2.2c), comma in a list
    (L.5.2a), after an opening part (L.5.2b), before and/but/so (L.4.2c).
  Our own word lists (misspellings, homophones, confused pairs, irregular verbs and participles, regular verbs, adverbs,
  irregular plurals), null-prototype lookups (a passage may say "constructor"). Grade presets (K: capitals and end
  marks; more kinds each grade). Planting is seeded (the same text, kinds, count and seed plant the same mistakes),
  kinds take turns, a sentence with fewer mistakes goes first, two mistakes never overlap or (when there is room) touch,
  and a mistake stays inside one paragraph, at most 4 words. **Re-roll** keeps pinned mistakes; **re-roll one**,
  **remove**, **pin**; a teacher **selects words to mark their own**: the kinds that fit there (each with what students
  would see), or wrong words they type with a kind that takes that many words. **Checking:** a mistake counts when the
  student's words over it read as the teacher's text (spaces and curly quotes aside; a run-on or comma splice also
  mended with "; " or ", and/but/so"); a correct word the student changed is reported ("That doesn't cost you
  anything, but take another look"), never counted.
- **The builder** (calm, as the owner asks): the set's name, Save, Print and one ⋯ More (Try it as a student, What
  students get, Start a new set); a "Mistakes to plant" card (grade, a chip a group, More kinds with every kind and its
  code, how many, Plant / Re-roll); passage tabs; the passage with its mistakes highlighted and numbered, then the list
  (wrong → right, the why line, the kind and code, a ⋯ menu each: Pin, Re-roll this one, Remove) and an answer key
  preview. **Paste, or upload** a .txt (read in the page) or a Word or PDF file (`BRB.textFromDoc`, new: the text read on
  the server with Crossword's readers and limits, 2 MB, 5 pages, 10 files a day, **no AI**; grown-ups who may host, never
  a kid or a student; the family grown-up fence refuses it). A long text is split into passages at paragraph ends. The
  draft saves itself to the game save ("Keep working on my draft").
- **Saving and sharing:** `game_sets` through the existing routes (`SET_GAMES` gains `mistake-hunt` with
  `cleanProofItems`: strict keys, 1 to 8 passages, 40 to 1,500 characters each, 1 to 15 mistakes, 20,000 characters in
  all; the title, the text, every wrong word and a why line through the site's text filter, and a text the filter or the
  game's tidying would change is refused, never changed, since the mistakes point into it; every mistake by the same
  rules). The class code, link, QR code, Copy and Assign to class (`BRB.assign`, a one-step lesson). **My worksheets**
  (#492/#493's list: open in the builder under the same code, Print, ⋯ Answer key, Assign, Copy link, Duplicate,
  Rename, Delete with an inline confirm). Labels: "Inside a volcano: 2 passages, 7 mistakes".
- **Students** (phone first): tap a word, a sheet opens with the word in a box (Fix, Put it back, "Next word too" for a
  fix across two words, as a run-on needs); fixes show struck with the new words in green. **Check** ("You found 4 of 6.
  Keep going!", the sentences that still hold one, a changed correct word flagged); **Hint** lights the sentence ("A
  hint for the yellow sentence" and what to look at), then the kind and its why line; **Show answers** after a check when
  the teacher allows it. What students are told first: how many, how many of each kind, or nothing. Work is kept in the
  game save per set (not reused if the teacher changed the set). The end card (stars, each passage's count) sends one
  `BRB.gameOver({ won: true, score: % found })`: a lesson step done, the Classroom completion grade, as Crossword.
  Keyboard: every word is a button, Enter fixes, Escape closes; screen reader labels; 44 px buttons; the page's chrome
  follows the language's direction and the passage stays English, left to right.
- **Print** (`services/proof-print.js`, `BRB.print`): a worksheet a passage (kicker, Name and Date, title, the
  teacher's note, directions with the count, a legend of 8 proofreading marks drawn here, the wrong text double spaced,
  "I found ___ of N mistakes", the class code and link); then, for school staff only (403 `key` for anyone else), a key
  a passage (each fix in place, bold and numbered, and the list: wrong → right · kind (code) and the why line). Words
  from the game's own tables in the viewer's language. CSS in `public/css/app.css` (`.mhp-*`).
- **Standards:** a lesson step that opens a set (`chapter=s-…`) practises its mistakes' Common Core codes
  (`official-tags.js SET_CODES`, registered by `game-sets.js`; `stepGameCodes` / `stepGameCover`), so the class
  Standards tab counts them when a student finishes (the tab itself is still unlinked from the class page, 12 Nov).
- **Read aloud: deferred.** The site's TTS speaks only lines registered in a game's word table; passages are the
  teacher's text, so a "proof" context (by passage and sentence) is Phase 4. Registered as silent in `tts-lines.js`.
- **Not in Phase 1, seamed:** Phase 2: Power with AI passages, "Check my passage" and AI why lines (the set already
  keeps `m[].y`, a why line of the teacher's own, filtered, 140 characters; the page and print use it before the fixed
  line), and a graded `proofread` lesson step (the plan's `step_progress` shape; the checker already returns found,
  missed and changed per mistake). Phase 3: Oomba chat on a set and class insights (counts per kind come from the same
  mistakes and their codes). Later: a different version per student (the seed is already the planter's input), a time
  limit, a live class mode.
- **Owner decisions still open:** the name's trademark check; which AI tools (if any) go behind the Teacher plan in
  Phase 2; whether Phase 2's graded step replaces the game step; Spanish passages; whether students may see the why
  line after every miss or only once answers are released (Phase 1: in the hint's second step); a live class mode.
- **Tests:** `tests/unit/proof-core.test.js` (every kind plants and its key fixes the passage back exactly, every
  candidate; determinism; no overlap; pin, re-roll, re-roll one, remove, the teacher's own; checking; the text filter;
  the server's copy; the file, languages and registration), `tests/unit/proof-sets.test.js` (the cleaner, save, find by
  code, My worksheets routes, the frame's flags, print and the staff-only key, Hebrew, text from a document, the SDK,
  standards), `tests/e2e/mistake-hunt.spec.js` (Chromium: a teacher builds, marks, pins, saves, prints the sheet and key
  to a Letter PDF and finds it in My worksheets; a student on an iPhone 13 plays by class code to the end card). The
  cover (`scripts/covers/mistake-hunt.recipe.js`) and share picture.

## Mistake Hunt, Phase 2: AI passages, Check my passage, why lines, and a graded proofread step (22 Nov 2026)
Phase 2 of the plan the owner approved with the mockup. **Gating, the owner's recommendation accepted:** the game,
saving, print, the key and Assign stay free (like Crossword); the AI tools are for teachers only, free teachers with a
small daily cap and Teacher plan holders without one.

- **Who gets the AI tools** (`services/proof-ai.js aiAccess`): school staff and the platform admin. Never a student, a
  kid, a family grown-up (the grown-up fence also refuses the routes) or a guest; the AI never talks to students. With
  the Teacher plan (`teacherPlan(...).entitled`: their own plan, a trial, a grant or a school seat), a tester
  (`MANIPULATIVES_USERS`) or the platform admin: `plan`, no daily cap (the site's AI budget still applies). Every other
  teacher: `free`, **`config.proofAiFreePerDay` AI requests a day (3; `PROOF_AI_FREE_PER_DAY`)**, Power with AI and
  Check my passage together. Only a request that reaches the AI counts (a refused topic, or the AI resting, does not).
  The count is the in-memory day window the site's other daily limits use (Crossword's 10 files a day): a restart
  forgets it, judged fine for a soft cap. When it is used up the builder says calmly "You've used today's free AI
  passages. They come back tomorrow, or try the Teacher plan." with **Try the Teacher plan** (`BRB.openTrial`: the play
  page opens `/trial` after a tap; no price). While paid plans are off, the sentence ends at "tomorrow" and there is no
  link. Why lines are part of saving and are not counted.
- **One way to call the AI** for all three: `callAi` (the one 90 s budget, no SDK retries, one more try only when busy),
  `config.builderModel`, effort low, plain JSON read with `jsonIn` (no strict `json_schema`: #512), the AI budget pool
  ('free', `recordUsage`). A failure is one warn line (`logAiFail`: the user id, the tool, the kind, the status, how long;
  never the topic or text) and a calm answer with `ai: false` and a reason (timeout, busy, error, resting, filtered).
- **Power with AI passages** (`POST /api/games/:id/proof/draft`, `draftPassages`): a switch at the top of "Mistakes to
  plant" (off by default; on: Topic, Length short / medium / long, Passages 1 to 5, with the existing grade, kinds and
  count). The topic passes the word rules and must not name one of the teacher's students (`namesIn` against the
  rosters of the classes they teach or run): refused before the AI ("Names never go to the AI"). The AI writes ONLY
  clean, correct, original, kid-appropriate passages; each is tidied (curly quotes, dashes), must be 40 to 1,500
  characters and pass the site's text filter **unchanged**, or it is dropped; then **proof-core plants the chosen
  mistakes on the server** with the builder's own planter, so the key is the AI's own clean text. The passages fill the
  empty passage tabs and then new ones (up to 8), the set's name becomes the topic if it had none, and each shows the
  label **"Written with AI. Read it before you save."** (kept until the teacher edits the text; not saved). When the AI
  fails or rests: "Oomba couldn't write passages this time; paste your own or try again." Judgment call: no starter
  passage library yet (the plan's fallback); the paste box is always there.
- **Check my passage** (`POST .../proof/scan`, `scanPassage`), on the paste screen beside "Use this text": the AI lists
  real mistakes in the teacher's "correct" text; the server keeps only flags whose words occur exactly once in it (with
  their offset), a filtered suggestion and a reason. The page lists each (wrong → suggestion, the reason) with
  **Accept** and **Ignore**; nothing changes unless accepted, and an accepted one replaces only its own words. Names
  are checked first, as for a topic.
- **AI why lines** (`POST .../proof/why`, `whyLines`): pressing Save with mistakes that have no why line of their own
  asks the AI once for all of them (the sentence with its mistake, what students see, the right words, the kind). The
  lines go into the mistake list as editable boxes marked "Written with AI" with "Oomba wrote these why lines. Read and
  edit them, then press Save."; the next Save saves. Each line is at most 140 characters and passes the filter, or is
  left empty (the fixed line a kind stays). Stored as the set's why lines (`m[].y`, the Phase 1 seam) with `ai: 1`
  (`cleanProofItems` now allows `ai`, only as 1). Any mistake's line can be edited later from its ⋯ menu ("Edit the why
  line"). If the AI can't, the set saves with the usual lines and says so.
- **A graded proofread step.** "Assign to class" (the builder's share box and My worksheets, as before) opens
  `/teach/assign`, which for the teacher's own Mistake Hunt set now offers **Hand in for a grade** first (the set's name,
  passages and mistakes; class, Opens, Due, **Show answers after the due date**, off by default and needing a due date;
  "Students get this set as it is now...") and "Practice in the game instead (no grade)" folded below (the Phase 1 game
  step). `POST /api/teach/assign-proofread` (`services/proof-steps.js assignSet`): school staff, their own set, a class
  they teach; a lesson of kind `proofread` with one step of kind `proofread` (`lessons.PROOF_KIND`, in
  `SNAPSHOT_KINDS` and the new `HANDIN_KINDS` with figures), assigned with its dates. **No migration**: the step's
  `items` is the snapshot `{ tell, passages: [{ t, x, g, m: [{ a, b, w, k, y }] }] }`, `show_answers` is 0096's column,
  `step_progress` holds the work. Later edits or deleting the set change nothing; a copied lesson keeps the snapshot and
  the switch; the step editor shows "2 passages · 7 mistakes" and only title, minutes and instructions.
- **Students play it in the game** (phone first): the lesson card says how many passages and "Fix the mistakes, then
  hand in. Handing in is final." with **Start** (then Keep going) to `/play/mistake-hunt?lesson=&step=`. The play page
  marks that lesson context `proof` and the frame gets `INIT.proofStep` (`proof-steps.js viewFor`): **only the words
  students see** (`[word, space]` pairs, no mistake marks, no correct text, keys or why lines), how many mistakes (or by
  kind, per the set's "what students are told") and their saved fixes. The game's graded mode reuses the tap-to-fix
  sheet; there is no Check, no hints and no Show answers (they need the key); fixes save as they go ("Saved");
  Previous / Next passage; **Hand in** asks in the page (no browser dialog) and is final. `POST
  /api/progress/:cl/:step/proofread` (`progress.proofAnswer`): every fix inside its passage, at most 6 words and 80
  characters, through the site's text filter (a student can't post words through it), no overlaps. Hand in marks each
  mistake once with proof-core's checker (the game's rules, so a run-on mended with ", and" counts).
- **Scoring:** `marks` is one character a mistake in reading order (passage by passage, '1' found, '0' missed), `score`
  = the share of mistakes found (%), label `proofread`. **Changing correct words costs nothing** (as in the game): the
  count is shown to the teacher ("Right words changed") and the student sees those words in rose under "See my work",
  never taken off the score. The end card: "You found 5 of 7 mistakes (71%)", each passage's count, and when the
  answers open "See the answers" (each mistake fixed, found or not, with its why line); "See my work" shows the
  student's fixes, green where they found one.
- **Answers never reach a student early:** the key and why lines are in the JSON, the frame and the lesson page only
  when the teacher's switch is on, the due date is over (the school's time zone) and that student has handed in
  (`figures-steps.reveals`, reused). The tests check the correct text, the why lines and any key are absent otherwise.
- **Teachers:** the lesson's progress page has a panel per proofread step: "Show answers after the due date" (the
  figures switch, `setShowAnswers` now takes both hand-in kinds), "N of M handed in", "% of mistakes found", **By kind of
  mistake** (each kind with its Common Core code, found and missed counts and a bar; counts for the whole class, never a

  count it like a quiz or figures step (one point a mistake). The class Standards tab credits each mistake's Common Core
  code from the snapshot, right or not per student (`standards-ccss.js`, as quiz items).
- **13 locales:** the game's new words (its I18N block) and the server's `proof.*` and `lessons.kinds.proofread`.
- **Not in Phase 2:** hints in the graded step (the mockup's Hints switch: hints need the key, so a graded hint would be

- **Owner decisions open:** whether 3 a day is the right free cap; hints in the graded step; whether the graded step

## Mistake Hunt, Phase 3: Oomba's chat on a set and class insights (22 Nov 2026)
Phase 3 of the plan the owner approved with the mockup (the Oomba panel beside the builder, the AI card on the results).
**Gating:** both are **Teacher plan tools** (`services/proof-ai.js planTools`, toolAccess's people: Teacher plan holders,
a trial, a grant or a school seat, testers on `MANIPULATIVES_USERS`, the platform admin): `'yes'`. A teacher without the
plan sees a calm "part of the Teacher plan" note with **Try the Teacher plan** (`/trial`, no price) while paid plans are
on (`'plan'`); while plans are off they see nothing new. Students, kids, family grown-ups and guests never. The Phase 2
tools (Power with AI, Check my passage, why lines, the free daily cap) are unchanged.

- **Oomba's chat on a set** (`services/proof-chat.js`, the Manipulatives chat's pattern, `services/manip-chat.js`).
  An **Oomba** button in the builder's head opens the panel. The game is its own sandboxed page, so the panel lives in
  the game (mirroring `public/css/manip-chat.css` in the game's tokens rather than sharing the file): 900 px and wider, a
  panel docked on the end side (380 px, 340 px under 1100 px) and the builder narrows beside it; narrower, a sheet over
  the lower part of the page with Minimize and Close, minimized to the round Oomba bubble at the bottom end corner with a
  dot when an answer came meanwhile. Escape minimizes; focus to the composer, the bubble, or back to the button. Closing
  while Oomba answers minimizes. Leaving the builder hides it. The teacher's words in Mint on the end side, Oomba's on a
  card with its mark; first-message ideas ("Fewer comma mistakes", "Make passage 1 easier", "Add a passage", "Only
  spelling"; on an empty set two topic ideas). The composer is a button, not a form: the sandboxed frame may not submit
  forms. The frame talks through the play page (`BRB.proofAsk` ops `chat`, `chat-get`, `chat-applied`), never directly.
- **What Oomba knows** (built on the server from the draft the page sends, `cleanDraft` then `setContext`): the set's
  title, grade, chosen kinds and how many a passage, each passage's correct text and its planted mistakes (kind, what
  students see, the right words). A passage the set could not keep (the game's tidying, the length limits, the text
  filter) is left out. A title or passage that fails the word rules or **names one of the teacher's students** is hidden
  from the AI (`{ hidden: true }`), and the AI is told to keep it with `{ keep: n }`. Never anything about students. The
  teacher's message passes `textProblem` and `namesIn` before anything is stored or sent; a refused message keeps its
  words in the box with the reason.
- **What Oomba can do.** Plain JSON (no strict schema): `{ reply, action: null | { op: 'replace', set: { title, grade,
  kinds, perPassage, max, passages: [{ keep: n, title?, count? } | { title, text, count? }] } } }`. **The AI never
  writes or places a mistake.** A kept passage's text comes from the teacher's own draft; a new one goes through
  `cleanPassage` (tidied, 40 to 1,500 characters, the text filter unchanged, no student's name) or is dropped; then
  **proof-core plants** the chosen kinds (`plantCapped`: `max` caps a kind, a group or a family such as `commas`,
  `capitals`, `apostrophes`, `homophones` in each passage, so "fewer comma mistakes" is a cap, not a guess). A kept
  passage under the same kinds and count keeps its mistakes, why lines and pins exactly; otherwise it is planted again
  (pins kept). Wrong words go through the filter. Any "mistakes" the AI sends are ignored. If nothing usable comes back,
  the set is unchanged ("Oomba's passages couldn't be used"). The builder puts a change in as **one change**: the whole
  set (name, grade, kinds, count, passages), "Oomba's change is in your set.", new passages labelled "Written with AI.
  Read it before you save.", and under the reply **Undo Oomba's change** (then **Put it back**). A change that arrived
  while the page was closed is offered once as "Put it in my set". Why lines are drafted again on the next Save.
- **A turn is a job** (one at a time per set, 409 `chatBusy`); the page asks every 2 s; a refresh shows the same wait; a
  restart ends the turn as failed. One AI call per turn (`callAi`, the one 90 s budget, `config.builderModel`, effort
  low, max_tokens 6000, the AI budget pool); every failure is one warn line without the teacher's words and a calm answer
  ("Oomba couldn't answer this time; your set is unchanged", and its timeout, busy, resting and restart sentences) with
  Try again and Edit. Rate limit: the Phase 2 `proof-ai` bucket (30 an hour).
- **Kept** (migration `0105_mistake_hunt_chat`, `proof_chats`): one conversation per teacher and set (the saved set's
  id, or `new` until the first save, which takes it over within 30 minutes), the newest 20 turns, 8 to the AI, the built
  set only on the newest 3 changes. Deleted with the set (`game-sets remove`, and pruned when the set is gone), after 60
  days untouched, and with the account (`game-sets forgetUser`, the users foreign key).
- **Class insights: "Oomba's read"** (`services/proof-insights.js`, `views/proof-step.js proofInsightHtml`), a card in
  each graded proofread step's panel on the lesson's progress page, above "By kind of mistake". **Only counts go to the
  AI:** for each kind of mistake in the set its found and missed totals across the students who handed in, its Common
  Core code, how many handed in out of how many, the grade and the number of passages. Never names, never a student's
  work or edits, never one student's result, never the passages. The AI writes `{ read, tips }` (two or three sentences,
  one or two teaching ideas) in the teacher's language, each line through the text filter. **The code's own read** is
  the fallback and is shown whenever there is no fresh read: "2 of 2 handed in. Together they found 36% of the
  mistakes.", "Missed most: ..." (the kinds missed most by share), "Found well: ...", and two ideas (a short set of the
  kind missed most, reading aloud and stopping at the next one). **Ask Oomba** (a data-api form, the page reloads):
  cached per assigned lesson and step (`proof_insights`) until a new hand-in arrives (hand-ins are final, so the count is
  the key) or the page is read in another language; "New work was handed in since Oomba's last read." A failure keeps the
  code's read with a calm toast. No rankings of students anywhere. `GET/POST /api/proof/insights/:cl/:step` (the class's
  managers; students and other teachers 404; a teacher without the plan gets `access: 'plan'` and 403 `teacherPlan`).
- **13 locales:** the game's new words (its I18N block, `chat*`, `idea*`) and the server's `proof.insight.*`.
- **Judgment calls.** The panel is mirrored inside the game rather than reusing `public/js/manip-chat.js`: the game is a
  sandboxed frame without the site's CSS or modules, so sharing would need the site's tokens and `api()` there. Empty
  passage tabs are not part of what Oomba sees, so a change drops them. Insights are generated on demand, not when a
  hand-in arrives, to keep AI use to what a teacher asks for. Insight rows hold no names; they are not deleted with a
  lesson yet (they are keyed by the assigned lesson and are unreachable once it goes).
- **Tests:** `tests/unit/proof-chat.test.js` (a reply-only turn and what the AI sees, no student names; a hidden passage
  kept; a replace re-planted by proof-core with the key fixing each passage back, the AI's own mistakes ignored, the set
  saving as it came back; caps, only spelling, an easier passage; filtered passages dropped; bad JSON and a timeout with
  Try again and a warn line without the words; a name refused before the AI; free teachers, students, kids and plans
  off; one turn at a time and a restart; the chat following its set and going with it and the account; insights with
  counts only, cached until a new hand-in, the fallback on failure, the plan note, students refused),
  `tests/unit/proof-chat-browser.test.js` (Chromium: the laptop panel docked beside the builder, a new passage as one
  change, Undo and Put it back, Escape; the iPhone 13 sheet and bubble; the plan note; the progress page's card before
  and after Ask Oomba). `proof-ai.test.js` checks the frame's new `chat` field.
