## Classroom dashboards: Eyes up on top, class lists on a layout switch, sent tools' names (22 Nov 2026)

Three things found while filming the dashboard promo.
- **Eyes up covers everything on a student's screen.** The card was a `position:fixed` box at z-index 60 inside the
  dashboard, so a student's open tool sheet (app.js `sheet()`, z-index 80, appended to `<body>`) sat on top of it: only
  the page's edges went dark and the student could keep using the tool. A tool filling the screen (the Fullscreen API,
  or `.gb-max` at z-index 1000) and any `<dialog>` or popover in the top layer were above it too. Now `#dash-eyes` is a
  `<dialog closedby="none">` opened with `showModal()` (public/js/dash.js `eyes`): in the top layer, shown last, so it is
  over all of them, and everything under it is inert (nothing can be tapped, clicked or reached by keyboard). Escape,
  its own close request and a tap outside do nothing; a key never reaches a sheet under it (`sheet()` closes on Escape);
  if it is closed by anything but the teacher it opens again, and a tool going full screen while it is up puts it back
  on top. Nothing under it is closed or changed, so the sheet, the tool in it, its scroll and a tool filling the screen
  are all as they were once the teacher ends it. The z-index is only for a browser without `showModal()`.
- **No "No students" after a layout switch.** The live check sends class jobs' names (`crew`) and the points for each
  student only for the widgets of the layout on screen, and the board asked for it only every 4 s, so for up to 4 s
  after a switch the scoreboard said "No students in this class yet." and class jobs "No students yet: add names...".
  Now the board asks at once after a switch, and after a save that adds such a widget or turns the scoreboard to
  students (`needsLive`); checks are numbered so an older answer arriving late is dropped. Until the names are there,
  both widgets say "Getting the class list..." (`dash.w.score.loading`, `dash.w.jobs.loading`, all 12 locales that have
  the widgets), with no class total of 0, no job "Open", and Next week and Shuffle disabled; the settings' jobs editor
  says the same. The empty state shows only when the server says the class has no students.
- **A sent tool is named as its widget is.** A tool with modes reached students named by its mode ("Geoboard", "Angle
  maker", "Fraction, decimal, percent", "3D shapes and nets") while the teacher's widget says the tool's name ("Shape
  board", "Fractions", "Geometry"): every tool with modes had the mismatch. `toolName` is now the tool's own name
  everywhere a sent tool is named (the student's banner, tray and copy, with the tool's icon, and the teacher's push
  list and "sent" toast). Build it sets keep their mode's name (`modeName`): the teacher's "Make a set" sheet names the
  mode too, so the two screens agree there.
- **Test:** `tests/unit/dash-film-fixes-browser.test.js` (Chromium, a student on an iPhone 13): Eyes up is on top at the
  middle and corners over an open sheet, taps, clicks and Escape reach nothing, and the sheet is as it was afterwards;
  the same over a copy filling the screen and a question box; a layout switch on a slow network never shows the empty
  text and the names come at once; the banner, tray and copy titles equal the teacher's widget titles in every mode.

## Mistake Hunt: free AI cap, hints, assign choice (22 Nov 2026)
Three owner decisions on the Phase 2 and 3 open questions.

**1. The free cap.** Owner: "3 free AI requests a day is fine, just make sure there isn't a way to get around that."
Holes found and closed:
- **The count was in memory** (`services/ratelimit.js`, the Phase 2 note "a restart forgets it"): every deploy or
  restart gave every free teacher a fresh 3. Now it is in the database (migration `0106_mistake_hunt_limits`,
  `proof_ai_days`: one row per teacher and **UTC calendar day**, `n` requests; the count starts again at midnight UTC,
  rows older than 8 days are pruned). Judgment call: a calendar day rather than a rolling 24 hours, because the page can
  say "today" and it is one row a day. `services/proof-ai.js take()` spends one with a single conditional upsert
  (`... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET n=n+1 WHERE n<cap`, better-sqlite3, synchronous) before the first `await`, so two
  requests at once can never both take the last one (it would hold across processes too). `left()`, which the page's
  "N free AI requests left today" number comes from (`aiInfo` in the frame, `left` in every answer), reads the same row.
- **Why lines took any text** (`POST /api/games/:id/proof/why`, up to 60 items, "not counted"): a free teacher could
  send any passage for unlimited AI. Now every passage Oomba drafts (Power with AI, for every teacher) is remembered as a
  hash (`proof_ai_drafts`: sha256 of the exact text, never the text; kept 7 days; deleted with the account). For a free
  teacher why lines are free only when every item's passage is one Oomba drafted for them in the last week; if any is
  not (pasted, uploaded, or edited after Oomba wrote it), the call costs one of the day's requests and is refused with
  `cap` (429) when none are left. At the cap the builder saves with the usual lines and says "You've used today's free
  AI requests, so the set uses the usual why lines." Plan holders, testers and the admin: unchanged, no cap. Recording
  for plan holders too means a lapsed plan keeps a week's free why lines for passages Oomba wrote.
- **Checked, no hole:** Oomba's chat (`proof-chat.js`: `current`, `send`, `applied` all need `planTools` `'yes'`) and
  class insights (`proof-insights.js ask`: `'yes'` only; the GET card makes no AI call) are Teacher plan only. Text from
  a document (`text-from-doc`) uses no AI. Crossword's AI clues answer only the Crossword game. A refused topic, a name,
  or the AI resting spends nothing; a request that reaches the AI counts even if the AI then fails (as before).
- **Not prevented:** one person with several free accounts gets 3 a day on each. Nothing is built for that (owner's
  call); the site's AI budget still caps the total.

**2. Hints on a graded hand-in.** Owner: "Allow teachers to choose whether hints can be used." The hand-in form has
**Allow hints** (off by default). It is kept in the step's snapshot JSON (`lesson_steps.items`: `{ tell, hints: true,
passages }`; no migration for the setting, a copied lesson keeps it) and sent to the game in `viewFor` (`hints`,
`hintsUsed`). A hint needs the key, which never reaches the student's page, so **the server answers it**: the game's
Hint posts the fixes so far with `hint: i` (`progress.proofHint`, `proof-steps hintFor`), the fixes are saved, and the
answer is the sentence (word indexes over what students see) with the first mistake in reading order not fixed yet and
its kind. The card says where to look; asking again for the same sentence adds the kind of mistake and the usual line
for that kind (never the set's own why line, which can give the answer away). Nothing left to hint: "No more hints for
this passage.", not counted. Each hint is counted by the server in `step_progress.hints` (migration 0106; at most 99; the
page can never send a count) and saved with the work. The teacher's progress panel says **Hints: allowed** or **Hints:
off** and, when allowed, a Hints column with a plain count per student ("2 hints"), in roster order, never a ranking;
the lesson editor and the teacher's lesson page say the setting too. Hints never change the score. Check and Show
answers stay off in graded play.

**3. The Assign page makes the teacher choose.** Owner: "When the teacher assigns it, they should have to choose this."
`/teach/assign` for a Mistake Hunt set now shows "How will students do it?" with two cards and nothing picked: **Hand in
for a grade** ("Students do it once in the lesson. It is marked and goes to the gradebook.": class, Opens, Due, Show
answers after the due date, Allow hints) and **Practice** ("Students play the set as often as they like. Nothing is
graded.": class, Due). Only the picked option's form shows. The radios belong to no form, so nothing can be sent before
a choice. No script: CSS `:has()` (inside `@supports selector(:has(*))`); a browser without `:has()` shows both forms,
each under its own heading, and the button pressed is the choice (the forms are the site's `data-api` forms, which need
the site's script anyway). The old folded "Practice in the game instead" is gone. **Printing never needs assigning:**
Print stays in the builder and on each saved set in My worksheets.

- **13 locales:** the server's `proof.assign.*` and `proof.step.hints*`, and the game's `hintNone` and `whyCap`.
- **Tests:** `tests/unit/proof-ai.test.js` (the count survives the in-memory limiter's reset and the frame reads it; a
  calendar day and pruning; three requests at once with one left, one through, also over HTTP; why lines free for
  Oomba's passages, a foreign or edited passage costs one and is refused at the cap before the AI, old drafts expire,
  plan holders uncapped), `tests/unit/proof-step.test.js` (the Assign page: two choices, none checked, no radio inside a
  form, each form in its pane, Allow hints off; hints off by default and refused; allowed: the snapshot round trip, the
  frame, the hint's sentence and kind, saved fixes, the count, nothing to hint not counted, bad indexes, a count the
  page sends ignored, the 99 ceiling, handed in, the teacher's pages), `tests/unit/proof-browser.test.js` (Chromium:
  no form before a choice, only the chosen one after; a student on an iPhone 13 taps Hint, sees the sentence, then the
  kind, and the server counts 2).

## Figures: Oomba's chat and the shared chat engine (22 Nov 2026)

The owner: Figures should be "hooked up to AI the same way Manipulatives is", with "a chat on the side where the teacher
can refine and adjust the draft if they don't like the initial output". Then GO on the design with four calls: no silent
starter set when the AI rests or fails on a first draft (one "Add a starter set instead" button); on a laptop with the
chat open, a "Questions | Print preview" switch; keep the Worksheet/Test toggle on the menu's box; build ONE shared chat
engine (server service and client component) that Figures uses now and the site-wide teacher companion uses next.

- **The shared engine** (`server/services/oomba-chat.js`, `public/js/oomba-chat.js`, `public/css/oomba-chat.css`). A
  surface is defined once with `defineSurface({ id, live, steps, may, context, check, quote?, answer, undo? })`: who may
  use it, the context a key names (only the teacher's own), the word and name checks, what a message quotes, the AI call
  (`answer` returns the reply and an `apply()` that writes), and undo. The engine does the rest the same way for every
  surface: one conversation per teacher, surface and context key (`oomba_chats`); each message a job (`oomba_turns`)
  answered in this process apart from any request, with progress (the surface's steps and when each began) and an
  estimate from the surface's own timed turns; the one-live-turn rule is the surface's (`live: 'owner'` one per teacher,
  `'chat'` one per conversation) held by a partial unique index on `live_key`; `apply()`, Oomba's turn and the job's end
  in one transaction, only while that attempt is still current (an `apply()` that throws is rolled back and the turn
  fails calmly); `handOff()` at shutdown and `recover()` at boot (a recent turn runs once more, an older one ends as
  failed 'restart' with Try again); `ready()` and `dismiss()` for "finished while you were away"; `prune()`, `forgetKey()`
  and `forgetUser()`. Exports: `defineSurface, surfaceOf, send, current, undo, addTurn, ready, dismiss, eta, run,
  recover, handOff, busy, settled, allSettled, prune, forgetKey, forgetUser`. The client's `mountChat({ id, url, ensure,
  opener, sub, privacy, leave, hello, ideas, ideasAfter, placeholder, stepText, quoteText, change, changeLinks, note,
  extra, onAct, onAnswer, onUndo, onMode, onQuote, onSync, start })` draws the Manipulatives chat's panel: docked on the
  right from 900 px (the page narrows), a sheet above the tab bar on phones that minimizes to the Oomba bubble with a dot,
  Escape minimizes, the progress card while a turn runs, failed turns with Try again and Edit, "What changed" with Undo,
  and a quote above the message box. The Manipulatives and Mistake Hunt chats keep their own code for now; moving them
  onto the engine is a later change (their tables and pages differ, and moving them here was not trivial).
- **Migration** `0107_figures_chat` (0106 went to Mistake Hunt's limits first): `oomba_chats(owner_id, surface, ctx_key, turns, updated_at)` (unique per owner,
  surface and key) and `oomba_turns(chat_id, owner_id, surface, live_key, me_id, status, step, steps, attempt, error,
  created_at, started_at, ended_at, seen_at)`. Generic names on purpose: the companion chat uses the same tables.
- **Figures as a surface** (`server/services/figures-chat.js`). The first message on an empty worksheet or test drafts
  it; every later one adjusts it. The AI answers plain JSON (no strict json_schema: it hung in production for the
  Manipulatives) `{ reply, title?, grade?, units?, edits: [{ op: 'add', after?, item } | { op: 'replace', n, item } |
  { op: 'remove', n }] }`. n is the question's number as the teacher saw it, turned into its id at once, so a question
  moved, edited or deleted while Oomba thought is not mistaken for another. An item is a generator (`{ gen }`) or a
  figure question of its own; both go through the draft checks (`repairTestDraft` / `repairDraft`: OF.check, OF.solve
  answer keys, options, words; a bad one is replaced by its kind's generator and logged without the words). Units are
  the app's: every figure that takes a unit gets it and its answer is worked out again with OF.solve (a generator
  question without an answer key gets the key whose value equals its generator's answer). Questions the teacher did not
  name are never sent back through the AI. At most 12 added in one answer, 40 on a sheet. The reply's "What changed"
  lists added, changed and removed numbers, the units ("inches", from the browser's own unit names), title, grade, any
  repairs, and "Every answer worked out from its figure"; the page marks only the questions Oomba rewrote or added
  ("Changed by Oomba"; a first draft marks nothing) until the teacher edits them.
- **Undo** per turn (the newest 5 changes keep their undo data): each question goes back only while it is still as
  Oomba left it (a hash of its fields); one edited by hand since is kept and the card says how many were kept. A removed
  question comes back in its place; title and grade the same way.
- **What the AI gets**: the sheet's kind (worksheet, test or lesson's figure questions), title, grade and language, and
  each question numbered with its kind, data, question, answer type, options, answer key and worked answer; the figure
  catalog and the generators (the grade's band, every band without a grade); the conversation's newest 8 turns. A
  title, question or option that fails the word rules or names one of the teacher's students is "(left out)". Never
  classes, assignments, students' answers or results. The teacher's message passes the word rules and the name check
  before anything is stored or sent, and again when its job starts. "Ask Oomba about this" (a question's More menu)
  quotes it: the server builds the quote from the stored question ("About question 4: ...").
- **Limits**: one live turn per teacher across their worksheets (409 `chatBusy` for the same sheet, `otherBusy` with the
  other sheet's id); the figures-ai rate bucket (30 an hour, shared with the menu's box and the old drafts); one AI call
  per turn within the one 90 s budget (`services/ai-call.js`), the 'free' pool, `config.builderModel`, max_tokens 6000,
  effort low. The budget resting: the chat says "Oomba is resting right now, so nothing was changed. You can keep
  working by hand..." and the builder works as before. On an empty sheet a failed or resting first draft offers "Add a
  starter set instead" once (the generators the words point at, `templateItems` / `templateTest`, undoable); nothing is
  added by itself any more.
- **Kept**: the newest 30 turns per worksheet; finished jobs 7 days (for the menu's notice); a conversation untouched
  for 60 days goes; it goes with its worksheet (`deleteWorksheet`) and with the account (`figures.forgetUser`, and the
  users foreign keys). Teachers only (the Teacher plan gate, their own worksheets); students and kids never see it.
- **The page.** The menu's dark card is one "Describe what you need" box: Worksheet or Test, the grade, "Draft it";
  "Start from scratch" and "Blank test" are links under it (they replace "Draft with AI", "Start from scratch" and
  "Build a test"). It makes the worksheet or test (`POST /api/figures/start`; refused words make nothing) and opens the
  builder with the chat running. "My worksheets" shows "'...' is ready. Oomba finished it while you were away" (or that
  it couldn't finish) with Open it and Dismiss; opening the worksheet counts as seen. In the builder the "Power with AI"
  switch, the brief box and the test's topic, subject and count boxes are gone: the Oomba button opens the chat
  (`figure_prefs.ai` now remembers whether it opens by itself on a new, empty worksheet or test on a laptop; a lesson's
  figure questions start by hand). With the chat open from 900 px, a "Questions | Print preview" switch shows one half
  at a time. The privacy line under the message box: "Oomba sees this worksheet and your words, never students' names or
  work." 13 locales (`js.oomba-chat`, `js.figures-sheet`, `js.figures`, `figures.menu`).
- **Endpoints**: `POST /api/figures/start`, `GET|POST /api/figures/worksheets/:id/chat`, `POST .../chat/undo`,
  `.../chat/starter`, `.../chat/dismiss`. `POST .../draft` and `.../draft-test` stay one release for pages still open
  (the page no longer calls them; their service functions and tests are unchanged).
- **Also fixed**: `bandOf('')` read an empty grade as K-2 (`Number('')` is 0), so the test drafter without a grade only
  saw two K-2 generators; an empty grade is now every band.
- **Tests**: `tests/unit/figures-chat.test.js` (the migration; a first draft as a job with steps and an estimate and
  no names to the AI; a refine turn changing only 3 and 7 and the units with the answers worked out again; repairs,
  drops, the 12-question cap and remove; Undo keeping a question edited by hand; names and personal details refused
  before anything is stored, a question naming a student left out, the check again when a job starts; students, guests,
  teachers without the plan and other teachers refused; one live turn per teacher; bad JSON and a timeout with Try
  again; the budget resting and the starter set; a restart; the rate limit; the menu's box and the ready notice; what
  is kept; the answer reader; a second surface with one live turn per conversation) and
  `tests/unit/figures-chat-browser.test.js` (Chromium on a laptop and an iPhone 13). `figures-browser`,
  `figures-lesson-step-browser`, `figures-product` and `figures-lesson-step` now drive the chat and the menu's box.

## Oomba teaching companion, phase 1 (22 Nov 2026)

The owner approved the design and mockups (a bubble on every teacher page; a panel docked on the right on laptops, a
sheet above the tab bar on phones) with these decisions, built as a new surface of the shared chat engine (see "Figures:
Oomba's chat and the shared chat engine"):

- **Who** (`services/companion-settings.js companionFor`): the Teacher plan rule, `toolAccess(u) === 'yes'`
  (services/teacher-tools.js): the platform admin and testers (MANIPULATIVES_USERS) always; with paid plans on, staff
  with the Teacher plan; with plans off, testers and the admin only. `COMPANION=0` hides it from everyone; a school can
  turn it off for its staff. Everyone else gets no bubble and no upsell, never on a student or kid surface.
- **Where** (`views/layout.js companionPage`): every teacher page on every device; not on bare pages (games, live
  players, quest players), print pages, a student view of a lesson, or a page with its own Oomba chat (a Figures
  worksheet, the Manipulatives: two Oomba panels would fight over one side of the screen; deviation from "every page",
  noted for the owner). On the class dashboard's teacher screen (bare, opted in with `companion: 'dash'`) the bubble is
  the last thing in the layout bar, never over a widget, and hides in Projector, Eyes up and full screen. The page's
  Permissions-Policy allows the microphone (`self`) only on pages that show the bubble.
- **The loop** (`services/companion.js`): one conversation per teacher (`ctx_key 'main'`, New chat starts again); each
  message a job (one live turn per teacher). A real tool-use loop: `explainOomba`, `getPageContext` (page type and safe
  ids: a class's grade, subject and number of students; on the dashboard the layout's widgets with numbers, switches and
  choices only, never their text, and the widget library), `searchGames` (a curated metadata list for the official
  games, `services/companion-games.js`: grades, subject, topics, CCSS standards seeded from the Number Quest unit
  mappings in each game's notes, minutes), `searchBooks` (the Story Library; guided reading levels A to Z are mapped to
  its grade bands and Oomba says so), `searchLessons` (CS Quest lessons, Figures generators, dashboard templates),
  `proposeDashboardChange`, `startBuild`, `readUpload`, and the web search server tool. At most the school's steps per
  answer; the last call is made with `tool_choice: none`. The model is `COMPANION_MODEL` or `BUILDER_MODEL` (no model id
  in code); AI budget resting is the calm "resting" turn. Markers in the reply (`[[game:id]]`) become cards, only for
  things a tool returned in that answer.
- **Writes need a tap.** `proposeDashboardChange` only makes a confirm card (prefers changing an existing widget of the
  same type over adding a second); Apply writes it to the teacher's own layout of a class they teach (engine `addTurn`),
  Undo puts back what is still as Oomba left it; both audited (`companion.dash.apply`, `.undo`). Not now marks it.
  `startBuild` makes a hand-off card for the Builder, Figures or the Manipulatives; "Open the Builder" opens
  `/build/new?for=class&class=...` with the brief filled into "Your lesson" (or Figures' "Describe what you need"); the
  teacher presses the final button there (audited `companion.handoff`). **No "build a widget"** and no "My activity"
  widget: when no widget fits, Oomba suggests existing widgets or a combination.
- **Privacy.** Messages, uploads and transcripts go through the Builder's scrubber (builder/lesson.js `scrub`: the
  teacher's students' names, emails, phone numbers, links) before they are stored or sent; the reply is scrubbed too and
  held back if it fails the Builder's text check. Web search is on by default (per-chat switch, school switch,
  `COMPANION_WEB_SEARCH=0`), reuses builder/search.js (blocked sites, query screening, the admin search log, ai-budget
  cost tracking), sends no location; a search that looks personal or unsafe shows no sources and is logged redacted.
- **Uploads** (migration `0108_teacher_companion`: `oomba_chats.opts`, `oomba_files`). Documents through the Builder's
  lesson reader (PDF, .docx, .txt, .md; 5 MB; a PDF at most 10 pages; scans refused; the shared 20 a day; the name
  scrubber and keyword pre-filter); the file is not kept, its text (at most 10,000 characters) stays with the chat and
  goes with it. Pictures: made a JPEG of at most 1,600 px in the browser, cleaned on the server (photos.cleanJpeg: JPEG
  only, size limits, every metadata segment removed), then the AI check (the profile photo's rules plus "no people":
  any person refused with a kind message, never kept, audited); a picture that passes is kept only until the answer
  that reads it is done, never longer than a day (decided: the smallest retention that still lets Try again work).
- **Microphone**: tap to start, tap to stop ("Listening… audio isn't kept"); the clip goes to
  `POST /api/companion/transcribe` (services/stt.js `transcribe`) and the words land in the box to edit. A teacher
  allowance: Teacher plan staff on their own conversation, with the Studio's caps (clips a minute, clips a day, the
  site's minutes); the kid rules (a kid's own game) are unchanged. Upload mode only in phase 1 (the live WebSocket relay
  is tied to a game id; words appear when the teacher taps stop).
- **Per-school settings** (School page, Settings tab, its own form; `schools.settings.companion`, no migration): Oomba
  on or off, web search on or off, days a chat is kept (7 to 365, default 60), messages kept (4 to 40, default 20),
  messages sent to the AI (2 to 16, default 8, never more than kept), steps per answer (2 to 12, default 8), messages a
  teacher may send an hour (5 to 100, default 40). Out of bounds is refused, never clamped. A teacher in no school gets
  the defaults; one in several gets the strictest. The engine gained optional surface hooks for this (`clean`, `meta`,
  `limits`, `prune`), backward compatible with Figures.
- **Legal:** /privacy section (all locales), LEGAL_UPDATED 2026-11-22, docs/legal-review.md entry (lawyer review
  pending).

## Oomba teaching companion: one chat everywhere, and live speech (22 Nov 2026)

The owner, after reviewing phase 1: ONE Oomba bubble and panel across the app. The Figures worksheet chat and the
Manipulatives board chat are folded into the companion; the microphone shows words as the teacher speaks.

- **Conversation model** (chosen as recommended): one running companion conversation per teacher (the engine's
  `ctx_key 'main'`), with page-scoped artifacts. Every message carries the page it was sent from (`meta.page`: the
  worksheet's id, the board's tool and id, checked on the server: only the teacher's own worksheet, only a host's own
  board), and the "Sees:" line follows the page (an SPA page like the Manipulatives updates it as the teacher moves).
  Each worksheet keeps its own change history through the turns that changed it (`change.kind 'figures'` with the
  sheet's id and its own Undo data); each board change is put on the board by the page with its own Undo and Redo.
  The old per-worksheet Figures chats (`oomba_chats` surface 'figures') and per-board chats (`manip_chats`) start
  fresh: they are not shown any more, kept in the database until their own 60 days (pruned by the companion's job)
  and deleted with their worksheet, board and account. No worksheet or board data is touched.
- **Page tools** (services/companion.js `PAGE_TOOLS`, offered only on their own page): `editWorksheet` (the Figures
  workflow, unchanged, in services/figures-chat.js: readAnswer, checkItem/repairDraft, OF.solve recompute, untouched
  questions never re-sent, applyPlan/undoPlan by question id, starterPlan, quoteOf, workflowRules for the system
  prompt) and `changeBoard` (the Manipulatives workflow, unchanged, in services/manip-chat.js: boardContext,
  readAnswer/buildChange through sanitizeDraft and cleanState, pageBoard, workflowRules). `getPageContext` adds the
  worksheet (sheetContext) or the board. On the live room's teacher view Oomba knows it is there and changes nothing
  (as before: the old chat was never in the room).
- **Routing**: on those pages the system prompt says the page tool is only for requests about what is on that page;
  anything else (a book, a game, the dashboard, how the site works, a teaching question) goes to the general tools and
  leaves the page as it is; when it can't tell, it asks one short question and changes nothing.
- **Writes, stated consistently**: a dashboard change needs the teacher's Apply tap (then Undo); a worksheet or board
  change is made at once when the teacher asks for it on that page, with Undo (the existing behavior of those chats,
  kept); builds are hand-offs the teacher finishes.
- **Names**: one rule everywhere: the teacher's students' names, emails, phone numbers and links are taken out of the
  message before it is kept or sent (the Figures and Manipulatives chats used to refuse such a message instead), and
  the words are checked again when the job starts (a student who joined meanwhile ends the turn as 'names'). Question
  text, board steps and titles naming a student are left out of what the AI sees, as before.
- **One panel**: the separate panels are gone (`public/css/manip-chat.css` removed; `public/js/manip-chat.js` is now the
  board's adapter; `public/js/figures-sheet.js` registers the worksheet's). Pages meet the panel through
  `public/js/oomba-bus.js` (`setPage(adapter)`: the page context, what goes with a message, ideas, the change card, the
  page's buttons, "Ask Oomba about this" quotes, Undo, the Questions | Print preview switch on laptops). Figures' menu
  "Describe what you need" makes the worksheet and sends the companion's first turn on it (services/companion.js
  `startSheet`); its "finished while you were away" notice reads the companion's unseen endings (`readySheets`; a
  background load peeks without marking them seen, and the bubble shows its dot). "Draft with AI" on a board opens the
  panel; the board's old drafter (Try again on a failed draft job) opens it with the words in the box.
- **Removed routes**: `/api/figures/worksheets/:id/chat` (and undo, starter, dismiss) and `/api/manipulatives/chat` (and
  applied); `/api/figures/worksheets/:id/ready/dismiss` added. The `figures` engine surface is no longer defined.
- **Live speech** (services/stt-live.js `companionRoute`, `/api/companion/listen`): the Studio's live relay with a
  teacher allowance, its own path and gate (`teacherGate`: companionFor, so the toolAccess rule and the school's switch),
  the same caps; the kid route and its rules are unchanged (the Builder check stays for every kid session). The page
  streams the mic as PCM (public/js/stt-worklet.js), shows the words so far greyed and read-only in the box, and they
  settle as final, editable words. Stops on a tap, on Send (no more words go in), when the panel closes, when the page
  is hidden, and at the longest recording (2 minutes, or STT_MAX_SECONDS if shorter). MediaRecorder keeps the clip in
  memory only, for a one-time upload (`X-Live-Id`, not counted twice) when the live link fails.
- **Follow-up**: Mistake Hunt's chat (services/proof-chat.js, inside the game's teacher editor) is still its own; moving
  it onto the companion is a later change.

## Dashboard points: reasons, whole-class points, the student's view and Google Classroom (22 Nov 2026)

The owner asked: "For giving points to kids on the dashboard you should be able to pick what those points are for and
there should also be an option to give the whole class a point for something and it should be noted as something the
whole class received a point for as well as what the point was for (e.g. leadership, teamwork, focused, being kind,
setting a good example, working hard, participation etc... doesn't have to be that wording exactly but options for why
the point was awarded would be great) And this should be visible on the students account so that they can see. This
should also be available to be pushed to Google Classroom"

This builds on stage 5's "Points for each student" (the scoreboard's Each student mode).

- **Reasons.** A fixed, positive list of 12 (nobody types a reason, there is no minus), in this order: leadership,
  teamwork, focus, kindness, setting a good example, hard work, participation (the owner's examples first), then
  helping, listening, being responsible, trying something new, good ideas. The first version's keys (kind, helpful,
  teamwork, effort, listening, responsible, brave, creative) are kept as they were, so stored points read the same with
  no migration of rows; a request may also use a few other names (kindness, focused, hard-work...), stored under the
  key (`POINT_ALIASES`). **Decided:** a fixed, tidy grid (two or three columns of icon and word) rather than most-used
  first: the buttons never move, so a teacher's hand learns where Teamwork is. A tap on a student's row (the whole row
  is the button, "+1" shows it) opens the grid; one tap on a reason gives the point.
- **Whole-class point.** **Whole class** (where "A point for everyone" was) opens the same grid and gives ONE point to
  the class, stored as the class's own tally per reason (`dash_class_points`), never one point per student. It shows
  as "Whole-class points: 7" with its reasons, and is recorded as "The whole class earned a point for teamwork".
  **Decided:** the old "everyone" is replaced; a request still sending `user: 'all'` gets the class point. Points the
  first version gave everyone (one row per student) stay as each student's own and read as before.
- **History.** Every award is remembered (`dash_point_awards`: who gave it, the student or the class, the reason,
  when, and whether it went to Google Classroom) for at most a year and 2,000 rows per class. Undo takes back the
  latest matching award and its count (never below zero; a count stored before awards were remembered still drops).
  **Decided:** Start again clears the counts and the remembered awards together: a fresh start, so students don't see
  old awards under a total of zero. Start again moved into the Recent sheet (three buttons fit the smallest scoreboard
  in every language, and the rare, clearing action is one step further away).
- **The student's view.** On the student's own class page (`/class/:id`), a calm **My points** card, once the class has
  any points: their own total, their points by reason, their latest awards ("Teamwork, Tue, Nov 22"), the class's
  points with reasons and the class's latest awards, and "Only you and your teacher see your points." The Classes tab
  links to it ("My points: 3"). The in-dashboard student view keeps its own points and adds the class's. A student never
  sees another student's name, id or points and never a ranking (tested: another student's reason and count are never
  in the page). The students' total ("Class total") stays as it was.
- **Teacher and projector.** The teacher's list stays in the class list's order (by name), never ranked; one line on
  top says the class's points and every student's together; **Recent** lists the latest awards (names on the teacher's
  screen only). The projector hides names and each student's points as before and shows the class's points big, with
  their reasons when the box is tall enough, and the students' total under them.
- **Google Classroom.** When the class is linked to a Classroom course, the reasons sheet has "Also post to Google
  Classroom" (one switch per class, `dash_class.points_gc`, off by default). Without the announcements scope (or with a
  connection that stopped working) the switch is greyed out with "Allow posting in Google Classroom", the class's
  Classroom page (the existing allow and reconnect path). A whole-class point posts to the class stream "Our class earned
  a point for teamwork! 🎉"; a student's point posts "You earned a point for teamwork! 🌟" to that student only
  (`assigneeMode: INDIVIDUAL_STUDENTS`, `individualStudentsOptions.studentIds` with only their Google id, from the
  roster link `gc_roster`, else the id they sign in with). The words are fixed, in the teacher's language: no names, no
  counts, no rankings. The point is always saved first; Google never blocks it: after 2.5 seconds the answer is
  "Posting to Google Classroom..." and the post finishes on its own; a failure, a student not on the Classroom roster or
  the class's 10 announcements an hour (shared with the Classroom page's announcements) gives a calm line ("The point is
  saved."). Undo of a posted point deletes its announcement too (best effort). The sync log says only "Dashboard point"
  and whether it was for the class or a student.
- **Deleting.** Both tables go with the school (`services/school-delete.js`). Deleting an account removes the awards for
  that student; awards a teacher gave stay with the class, no longer saying who gave them.
- Migration `0109_dash_point_awards`. Tests: `tests/unit/dash-points.test.js` (with the fakes in `tests/support`), and
  `tests/unit/dash-stage5.test.js` where "everyone" changed. `npm run dash:fit` seeds whole-class points too, and
  `SIZES=stage5` checks only the stage 5 layouts.

## My points: the total on top (23 Nov 2026)

The owner chose layout A of three mockups for the student's "My points" card: "Let's go with A."

- **The card** (routes/schools.js `myPointsPanel`, public/css/schools.css `.mypoints`): the title "My points", then a
  Spark-tinted bar "All my points" with a small line "My own 4 + the whole class's 3" and the total big on the right
  (the student's own points plus the whole class's points), then two matching cards side by side: "Just me" (the big
  number, chips by reason, Recent) and "Whole class" (the same). A Recent row in the class's card shows the reason and
  the day; the full sentence ("The whole class earned a point for teamwork") stays as its screen-reader text and title.
  The footer "Only you and your teacher see your points." On phones (640 px and less) the two cards stack; nothing is
  wider than the screen at 375 px.
- **Unchanged:** never another student's name, id or points, never a ranking; the students' total ("Class total") is not
  on the card. The in-dashboard student view adds the same total line, "All my points: 7" (own + class), under the
  class's points.

## Points from the Oomba chat (23 Nov 2026)

The owner: "make sure that the teacher can add a point for a student from the oomba chat. Like 'give the whole class a
point for xyz' or 'give x student a point for xyz'". Student names never go to the AI.

- **Placeholders instead of names.** The companion's scrubber now puts a numbered placeholder where it takes out a
  student's name: "Give Maya a point for teamwork" is kept and sent as "Give [student 1] a point for teamwork"
  (builder/lesson.js `scrub` gained a `token` option; every other caller is unchanged and still gets "[student]"). Which
  students a number stands for (their account ids, never their names) is kept with the message on the server only
  (`meta._who`; the chat engine never shows meta keys starting with "_" to the page) and never goes to the AI. The same
  student keeps the same number for the whole conversation (Try again and an edited message keep theirs). A name that
  is not an account yet (a Google Classroom roster name waiting) stays a plain "[student]", which can't get a point.
  **On the teacher's own page** the names come back: the server puts each placeholder's student's current name (only
  the teacher's own students) into the teacher's messages and into any placeholder in Oomba's words, as it fills in the
  point cards (`dress`, `namesIn`). What is kept and what goes to the AI stay the placeholders. A placeholder standing
  for two students shows both names.
  **Decided:** a placeholder can stand for several students (a first name two students share); the server resolves it
  in the class, and asks when it is still more than one.
- **The tool** (`givePoint`, a general tool, not a page tool; services/companion.js `pointPlan`): target "class" or a
  placeholder, a reason (the 12 keys; close words are read: "working together", "kindness", "hard work"...), an optional
  class id from getPageContext. **Which class:** the one asked for, else the page's class (the dashboard, the class
  page), else the teacher's only class; for a student, the only class of this teacher the student is in (decided: better
  than asking when it is clear); else a class choice card. The AI gets back only "given" (to one student or the whole
  class, the reason), "waiting for the teacher" (what to pick) or why not. **Class names:** shown to the teacher on the
  cards; never in what this tool returns to the AI (they are teacher-written and could hold a name). At most 5 points in
  one answer; a worksheet change and a point are not mixed in one answer.
- **Giving.** Clear (one class, one student, a known reason): given at once when the answer is saved, through the
  dashboard's own `pointsAction` (the history, the Recent lists, the class's Google Classroom switch and its posting
  after the point is saved, the dashboard's hourly limit, the same bucket), audited `companion.point`. The card: "Gave
  BouncyPenguin51 a point for Teamwork" or "The whole class got a point for Teamwork", with Undo (the dashboard's Undo:
  the latest matching award and its Classroom post; audited `companion.point.undo`). The names on the card are filled in
  by the server for the teacher's own page (`dress`), outside Oomba's words. **Unclear** (two students match, an
  unknown reason, several classes): one short choice card with buttons; nothing is given until a tap; the tap gives it
  as a turn of its own with Undo. A name that is not one of the teacher's students (so not a placeholder), or a student
  not in the class: Oomba says so calmly and nothing is given.
- **Who:** companion access (companionFor) and a class the teacher teaches and runs (`D.isTeacher` and
  `S.canManageClass`); never an archived class.
- **The dashboard:** a point given or taken back from the chat on that class's dashboard asks for the points at once
  (an `oomba:points` event, the dashboard's own live check); other screens get it at the next check.
- **Privacy:** /privacy "Oomba, the teaching companion" says names become placeholders kept only on our servers, and
  that Oomba can give a point when the teacher asks, with Undo (all locales; LEGAL_UPDATED 2026-11-23,
  docs/legal-review.md). Tests: tests/unit/companion-points.test.js.

## Icons: Oomba geometric for controls, Fluent 3D for big spots (22 Nov 2026)

Follows "Icons: Fluent Emoji 3D". The owner felt the Fluent icons were "still too emoji" and compared six directions on
real pages (soft line tiles, brand circles, ink and spot, our own geometric set, soft 3D objects, and a hybrid). He chose
the hybrid: our own Oomba icons for every control, and the Fluent 3D pictures only for big decorative spots.
- **The rule, in the one helper.** `iconHtml` (and `ico`, `leadIcon`, `iconLine`, `setIcon`, `setLabel`, unchanged for
  their callers) draws an emoji below 40 px as its Oomba icon, and at 40 px and up as its Fluent 3D picture (tool cards,
  page headings, empty states, rewards). A name with no 3D picture keeps its Oomba icon at any size.
- **Content stays Fluent.** Animals, food, weather, characters, faces, hands as gestures, colour swatches and the like
  have no Oomba icon on purpose: they are pictures of things, not controls, and draw as before (3D at 28 px and up, Flat
  below). Avatars, game covers and anything people wrote were never icons and are unchanged. The 18 manipulative tool
  pictures stay.
- **The set.** 159 icons, drawn in `scripts/icons/oomba-art.mjs` and built by `scripts/icons/build_oomba.mjs` into
  `public/icons/oomba/<name>.svg` (one `<symbol id="i">` each) and `public/js/icons-oomba.js` (Fluent name to icon, and
  a cache version). 181 of the 249 Fluent names in the map are drawn; 68 stay Fluent as content. Their Fluent Flat files
  are no longer shipped, which keeps `public/icons` under its budget.
- **The style.** A 24-unit grid, chunky rounded shapes (corners about 2.5 to 3.5), strokes 2 to 2.6 with round ends,
  one brand color per icon (mint, spark, or coral for live, record and stop signals) plus ink. Spark yellow never
  carries the meaning alone (it is faint on cream): ink always sits on it, like the logo. The logo's owl eyes appear only
  on Me, Classroom and Eyes up.
- **Light and dark.** The page draws the icon as an inline `<svg><use href="/icons/oomba/<name>.svg#i">`, so the ink that
  sits on the page is `currentColor`: dark on cream, cream on the dark theme, cream on the black "current" pill. Ink on a
  colored piece is always #141414, so it reads on mint, spark and coral in both themes. The `data-fx` attribute names the
  Fluent picture the icon stands for (tests read pages through `tests/support/deicon.js`).
- **Landing.** The layout tour's titles, widget chips and dots, the "Why games work" cards and the how-it-works steps
  printed raw emoji; they go through the helper now. The hero live card's faces (the demo class) are Fluent pictures.
- Credits: `docs/media-credits.md` (the Oomba icons are ours; Fluent stays credited, MIT).

## Oomba companion: navigate-then-do and choice cards (23 Nov 2026)

Owner feedback after one chat everywhere (#532): the idea chips felt like a form, "open the dashboard and ask again"
felt like homework, and open questions made the teacher type what a tap could say.

- **A greeting, no chips.** The empty panel shows no example prompts anywhere (the companion, Figures and math boards
  alike). It greets the teacher by their own first name as the site shows it (`views/layout.js` gives the panel the
  signed-in teacher's display name, never a student's): "Good morning, Greg", "Back at it, Greg", "Happy Friday,
  Greg", then one short line such as "What can I help with?". `public/js/companion-greet.js` picks by the browser's
  local time (morning, afternoon, evening, night; Friday, Monday morning and the weekend have their own), seeded by
  the local date so it stays the same all day and never flickers. Without a name the plain form is used. All 13
  locales, written for each language rather than word for word. A page with its own line (Figures: "Ask for a
  worksheet..."; a math board: the tool in use) replaces only the second line.
- **Navigate-then-do.** When a request needs a page the teacher is not on, the AI calls `proposeNavigation`
  (`findMyPages` first when it needs ids) instead of telling the teacher to go there and ask again. The card says
  "I'll open the 3B dashboard and do this there", shows the request, and offers Go there and Not now. Targets are only
  the teacher's own pages: their classes' dashboards (where they are a teacher of the class) and class pages, their
  Figures worksheets and their math boards; never a student view. When several fit ("my dashboard" with two classes)
  a choice card asks which first; each option carries its target, so a tap makes the Go there card at once.
- **The request is carried server side.** Go there stores `pending = { page, request, at }` on the teacher's companion
  chat (the `opts` column; no migration) and navigates in the same tab. On load the page asks
  `POST /api/companion/resume` with the page it is on; only that exact page (type and class, worksheet or board id)
  runs it, once, as the teacher's turn, and the panel opens by itself. It expires after 10 minutes; Not now, a new
  Go there or a target that is no longer theirs clears it. Confirm-before-write and Undo are unchanged: on the
  dashboard the same Apply card appears without retyping. Go there is audited (`companion.nav`).
- **Choice cards.** For a decision with a few clear answers the AI calls `askChoice` (2 to 5 short options, names
  scrubbed like every other output). The card shows them as buttons plus "Something else", which puts the caret in
  the box. A tap is sent as the teacher's answer, as if typed; the card then shows the pick.
- **Client.** `oomba-chat.js` now redraws when any card's state changes (not only point picks), so Not now and a
  picked option show at once.
- Tests: `tests/unit/companion-nav.test.js` (greeting by hour, day and locale with only the teacher's name; Go there
  stored, resumes only on the matching page, once, and expires; Not now; the choice card's answer as a turn and as a
  target; scope: never another teacher's class or a student page) and `tests/unit/companion-nav-browser.test.js`
  (laptop and iPhone 13: greeting with no chips; School page to dashboard with Go there, the confirm card without
  retyping, Apply, Undo; two classes give a choice card first; Not now leaves nothing pending; no console errors, no
  sideways scroll).
## Oomba Figures 1.6.0: seven new chemistry kinds (23 Nov 2026)

The owner: "Watch this video end to end and include everything they have ... Also visit the site [the source's chemistry
site] and [its physics site] to make sure we have everything" (the sites' names left out, as docs/third-party.md asks), and then: "Update based on the repo if all of it is there."
The source project (the one ported since 1.1.0, docs/third-party.md) added seven chemistry generators after our port
at `3bb43190`; at `9ed3093` its chemistry site lists them beside the ones we have: Chromatography, Electrochemical
Cells, Phase Diagram, Bond Energy Curve, Equilibrium Graph, Rate Law Graphs and VSEPR Shapes. Every other generator on
that site is already in Oomba Figures. The physics generators it added (and the biology cladogram) are a
separate batch, 1.7.0.

- **A new version, like 1.5.0.** Oomba Figures 1.6.0 is a new version folder: the core and the same seven packs (no new
  pack; the chem pack gains `chromatography`, `galvanicCell`, `phaseDiagram`, `bondEnergy`, `equilibrium`, `rateLaw`
  and `vsepr`). 1.0.0 to 1.5.0 have shipped and stay byte for byte (the lock, and git at the 1.5.0 release); every
  catalog figure 1.5.0 drew draws the same bytes in 1.6.0 and checks and solves the same (`tests/unit/figures-v160.test.js`).
  New builds, the Builder's tags and the Figures product pin 1.6.0; the CSP, the scanner and the screenshot worker list
  the eight new files.
- **Ported: the science only.** Each new kind's pure logic is ported into `figures/src/ported/` with its note
  (`chromatography.js`, `cells.js`, `phase.js`, `morse.js`, `equilibrium.js`, `kinetics.js`, `vsepr.js`), from the
  source's state after its own review fixes (`6e613e8`: niceRange down to 0.000001, a·r₀ = 3 for the Morse wells, the
  zero-order data stopping before [A] reaches 0, ln[A] to 3 decimal places, XeOF₄'s O at the apex, radicals' angles).
  The checks, the answers (`OF.solve`), the label placement and every drawing are Oomba's own (`figures/src/
  chromatography.js`, `cells.js`, `phase.js`, `chemgraphs.js`, `vsepr.js`); no Svelte component, settings panel, page
  address, example or preview picture is taken.
- **Judgment calls.** VSEPR: the source builds each molecule from its Lewis structure engine, which is not ported (too
  large for one kind); Oomba has its own table of 48 molecules and ions (each one's central atom, outer atoms, bond
  orders, lone pairs and charge) and takes one's own `{ central, outer, lone }`, refused unless the electrons add up.
  The source's drag-to-turn view is `yaw` and `pitch`. Phase diagram: a lettered mark names a region ("liquid") rather
  than a temperature and pressure, since a real substance's diagram is not to scale and a point would be drawn where it
  is not; the place is found well inside the region, clear of the boundaries, guides and labels. The kind names fit the
  Canvas kit's 20 characters (`galvanicCell` for Electrochemical Cells, `bondEnergy`, `rateLaw`). Generators deal a
  metal by atomic number and a substance, mark, stress kind or molecule by its place in the kind's list, as the
  pedigree's mode is dealt, because the gen language's answers are numbers; the figures still take the words.
- **Grayscale.** VSEPR's ball-and-stick prints (and with `gray: true` shows) one gray per element, set apart by hand
  as the source does (C and O, N and H, S and F never print alike); the equilibrium and bond energy lines are told apart
  by dash as well as color; a chromatogram's spots keep their color with a darker edge, and dyes are matched by how far
  they traveled, so a gray copy still answers its questions.
- **Generators (21).** Rf of a dye, which known dye a mixture lacks (a spot of the same color at another height is
  another dye); E°cell from the potentials shown, the anode, the electrons' way along the wire, the anode's E° (negative
  answers); the phase at a lettered point, the change of state along an arrow, the triple point read off a grid
  (negative temperatures); the bond length, the energy at the bottom of the well (negative), the strongest bond; Kc from
  the graph's levels, the shift after a labeled stress, the stress that was made (hidden); the order from the three
  graphs, k from the ln[A] slope, the half-life. Each key is its figure's OF.solve value, and the generator audit
  (`figures-gen-audit`) checks the student sheet never shows the answer. Choice generators keep to 4 options (Oomba
  Canvas's self-test takes 2 to 4): the change of state is asked for heating (melting, vaporization, sublimation) and
  the VSEPR shape among bent, trigonal planar, trigonal pyramidal and tetrahedral. Number generators whose answers can
  be negative are checked in every language the way the Figures product deals them (the last worked line says the
  answer), since Oomba Canvas's keypad has no minus sign (`figures-gen-words`).
- **The product.** Catalog entries with presets (the first is each card's default, its switches that default on given
  as true so the editor shows them on), options and hide parts; names and descriptions and the new hide parts' names
  in the 12 site languages; the generators' words in all 13; figure words in 12; Builder trigger words and the template
  drafter's topics. The "Draw it" grid stays with the shapes and the coordinate grid: none of these figures is drawn
  corner by corner. Print, Assign and the lesson Figure step needed no change (tested).
- **Fixes to kinds already ported.** Every source commit since `3bb43190` was read. Only two touch code we ported:
  `88ba74d`/`6e613e8` move the heating curve's `niceRange` into shared code and let it reach steps down to 0.000001
  with tidied products (our `hcNiceRange` never sees spans that small, and its rounding already removes the noise, so
  the heating curve draws the same; the new kinds use the new range), and `0838979` writes a graph's corner numbers on
  their own lines when its axes meet at two different values (Oomba's axes always did). The rest are the new
  generators, examples, previews, help text in the settings panels (`f7be0c7`, `4e74759`), the physics generators'
  own fixes (`86d40c0`, `9e725a0`) and moving the pulley's support drawing into shared code (`f337ad2`; Oomba's pulley
  is its own). No fix applied to 1.6.0's older kinds, so they draw as in 1.5.0.
- **Tests.** figures-v160 (frozen versions, latest pin, byte-identical 1.5.0 figures, the new kinds in the frozen file),
  figures-chem16 (the science against known values, refusals, solve, hide, print grays, languages, the generators,
  worksheets with Assign and the lesson step), figures-chem16-words (12 languages and look-alikes), the generator audit,
  figures-gen-words, and the new editors in Chromium (figures-browser).

## Oomba Figures 1.7.0: seven new physics kinds and the cladogram (23 Nov 2026)

- **What the owner asked.** "include everything they have" and "Update based on the repo if all of it is there". The
  source project (docs/third-party.md, "ported") added eight generators outside chemistry since our port at
  `3bb43190`: circular motion, electric and magnetic fields, the lever, torque, the pendulum, the spring and the roller
  coaster on the physics site, and the cladogram on the biology site, with review fixes (`9e725a0`, `86d40c0`,
  `4e74759`) and shared support code (`f337ad2`). All eight are in, at `9ed3093`. Its seven new chemistry kinds are
  Figures 1.6.0, built at the same time on its own branch; this is 1.7.0 so 1.6.0 can merge first.
- **A new version, like 1.5.0.** Oomba Figures 1.7.0 is a new version folder: the core and the same seven packs (no new
  pack; physics gains `circularMotion`, `fields`, `lever`, `torque`, `pendulum`, `spring`, `rollerCoaster`; bio gains
  `cladogram`). 1.0.0 to 1.6.0 stay byte for byte (1.6.0 merged first and is frozen like the rest; 1.7.0 carries its
  chemistry too). Every figure 1.6.0 draws, its seven chemistry kinds included, draws the same bytes in 1.7.0
  (`tests/unit/figures-v170.test.js` compares against 1.6.0). Built by script only: until 1.7.0 ships, drop its lock entries and rebuild (`node -e` on
  `figures/SHIPPED.json`, then `node scripts/build-figures.js`; the command is in the commit message).
- **Ported: logic and layout; Oomba's own: data, checks, answers, drawing.** The source draws these figures from labels:
  its lever works out the effort, and its torque generator works out moments, but its circular motion, pendulum, spring
  and roller coaster compute nothing (k, v, h and the like are typed words). Oomba's data is numbers, so `OF.solve`
  gives the answers: v²/r and mv²/r and the tension at the top and bottom of a vertical circle; the field's direction
  and strength at a point; the effort and mechanical advantage; net torque, the balancing value and place, support and
  cable forces; the period 2π√(L/g), the drop L(1 − cos θ) and the speed √(2gh); kx, ½kx², series and parallel k;
  speeds on the track by energy, the fastest point and the loop's least height 2.5R; how many taxa share a trait, which
  trait came first, a taxon's closest relative.
- **Refused, not drawn wrong.** A car too fast over a hill or too slow at the top of a loop, a point on a charge, arms
  that do not suit the lever's class, a cable that would push, two supports in one place, a hanging spring given both a
  mass and an extension, a rough stretch (the speeds stop there: friction takes energy the figure cannot know), a mark
  naming a trait the tree has twice.

| Source item | Status | Oomba | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Circular Motion: top view (nothing, string, turntable, road; up to 8 places), vertical circle (string, loop, hill, dip), conical pendulum | Ported layout | `circularMotion` | Arrow sizes and contact forces ported; numbers, directions and drawing Oomba's. The source's notation choice (arrow over or bold) is left out. |
| Electric and Magnetic Field: one, opposite, like charges; plates; bar magnet; wire | Ported | `fields` | Field tracing ported; added: up to 4 charges of any size up to ±3 and named points with their field. |
| Lever: class 1, 2, 3; load as block or arrow; units | Ported | `lever` | Arms that do not suit the class are refused instead of swapped. Label sizes left out. |
| Torque: pivot, two supports, wall with or without cable; up to 6 loads; beam weight; masses | Ported | `torque` | Mirroring left out; the balancing place added. |
| Pendulum: one bob with forces, the swing with A, B, C | Ported layout | `pendulum` | Length, mass and g added for the answers. |
| Spring: hanging or horizontal; one, before and after, three positions; 1 to 3 springs in series or parallel | Ported coil | `spring` | k, extension and mass added for the answers; the layout is Oomba's. |
| Roller Coaster: points, loop, object, velocity, rough stretches | Ported curve | `rollerCoaster` | Speeds and the loop's least height added; the length mark under a rough stretch is a μₖ label only. |
| Cladogram: diagonal or rectangular; ready-made trees; blank names and traits; node numbers | Ported | `cladogram` | The tree editor's pointer edits become data (a nested tree, a ladder or letters); marks added for questions. |
| Shared support hatching, label placer, settings and address format | Not ported | | Oomba draws its own hatching and places its labels. |

- **Questions.** Three generators per kind, 24 in all, each answer its figure's `OF.solve` value: circular motion
  (centripetal acceleration, the net force, the acceleration's direction), fields (the field's direction at P by the
  right-hand rule, attract or repel from the lines with the signs hidden, which point is stronger), lever (the effort,
  the mechanical advantage, the class), torque (net torque, where a load must hang to balance, the force at a support),
  pendulum (the period, the speed at the bottom, the energy at the top), spring (F = kx, ½kx², a hanging mass's stretch),
  roller coaster (the speed at a point, where it is fastest, the loop's least height), cladogram (how many animals share
  a boxed trait, which of two traits came first, the closest relative). Words in all 12 other site languages, en-GB for
  anticlockwise and centre.
- **Judgment calls.** The net torque question keeps clockwise positive and, since the merge with 1.6.0, deals
  counterclockwise (negative) answers too, as `OF.solve.torque.net` is signed: Oomba Canvas's keypad has no minus key,
  so a number generator that can deal a negative answer is checked the way the Figures product deals it, by its last
  worked line in every language (`figures-gen-words`, the rule 1.6.0 brought). Choice generators keep 2 to 4 options
  for the Canvas self-test. "Draw it" (the dot grid) is for shapes and the coordinate
  grid only, so these kinds use the typed editor. The kind is `fields` (the source's name); the catalog calls it
  "Electric and magnetic fields".
- **Tests.** figures-phys17 (answers against the formulas, refusals, hide, grayscale print, languages, generators),
  figures-v170 (frozen versions, the latest pin, byte-identical earlier figures), the gen audit and the gen words.
