## Oomba companion: how-to answers with links, Create class and Copy (23 Nov 2026)

Owner example: a teacher typed "Can you make me a test classroom so I can check out your dashboard?" and Oomba said it
couldn't, with words to follow but no link and nothing to copy.

- **Create class (Oomba does it).** A `createClass` tool proposes a card: "Create the class “Test class”?" (the name
  the teacher gave, else "Test class" in their language; a grade only when they said one), with Create and Not now.
  Create makes the class through the same rule and service as My classes' New class (`canCreateClass`: admins, and
  teachers where the school lets teachers make classes; `createClass` with the teacher as its teacher; the same
  `class-new` hourly limit), audited (`class.create` and `companion.class.create`). No students are made and a
  student's name is never a class name. The answer then shows "Made the class ..." with Undo (deletes the class
  while it never had a student, as Delete on My classes does; a class with a student stays) and Open its dashboard
  (Go there with nothing to carry: the teacher lands on the new class's dashboard with the panel open). At more than
  one school where they may make classes, a choice card asks which. Where they may not, there is no card: the answer
  is numbered steps with links (ask a school admin).
- **How-to answers (Oomba explains).** `server/services/companion-help.js` is the one source of truth for steps: each
  task's steps name real pages (paths of the router) and real buttons (locale keys the site's own code uses), and
  `howTo` fills in the teacher's own links (their class, their school) and the labels in their language. Without one
  class in mind it starts with "Open your classes and open the class" and names tabs instead of linking. School
  settings for a teacher who isn't an admin, and anything for a teacher without a school, say who can do it. When
  one page covers the task the tool offers Go there.
- **Which requests are handled.** Done by Oomba: make a class (new), open a class, its dashboard, a worksheet or a
  board (Go there), dashboard changes, points, finding games, books and lessons, hand-offs to the Builder, Figures
  and the Manipulatives. Answered with linked steps: add students and their login cards, print login cards again,
  add a co-teacher (or invite a teacher to the school), assign a game or lesson, set due dates, host a live game,
  see progress and the gradebook, give students a Figures worksheet, school settings, connect Google Classroom (when
  it is on), find a book. Left as steps on purpose: anything that would send student names to the AI (adding
  students), invite people by email, change school settings, post to Google Classroom, or assign and grade (each
  has its own confirm page today; they may become tools later).
- **Links in answers.** The server keeps a Markdown link only when a tool gave that exact path in this answer (the
  teacher's own pages); every other link is cut to its words, as before. The page renders a small, safe Markdown
  (`public/js/oomba-text.js`): everything escaped, numbered and bulleted lists, bold, and links only to a same-site
  path (same tab) or https (a new tab). The conversation is kept, so a link and the way back lose nothing.
- **Copy.** Each Oomba answer (never the teacher's own words) has a small Copy icon button (aria-label "Copy"). It
  copies the words as clean text: steps numbered, links as "words (address)" with the site's address, no bold marks,
  citation numbers or buttons, and says "Copied" for a moment. `navigator.clipboard`, with a hidden text box and
  `execCommand('copy')` where that isn't there (older iPhone Safari, plain http).
- Tests: `tests/unit/companion-help.test.js` (every help page opens with 200 for a teacher, every label is in all 13
  languages and used by the site's code; steps and links per teacher; links an answer may keep; the Markdown
  sanitizer; Copy text; createClass's card, rule, audit, Undo, Open its dashboard, Not now, the admin-only school)
  and `tests/unit/companion-help-browser.test.js` (laptop and iPhone 13: the owner's exact ask, Create, the class,
  Open its dashboard, Undo; the admin-only variant's linked steps all 200; a how-to answer's link opens in the same
  tab with the conversation kept; Copy's clipboard text; no console errors, no sideways scroll).

## Story Library: the book maker (23 Nov 2026)

The owner: "Build this into Oomba in the reading section. This is a builder task where users can either upload a story
they want to make choose your own adventure or have ai generate an illustrated book that can either be a normal flowing
book or a choose your own adventure. Again, this should be an iterative build process like the normal builder...
starting off with a few generic options, then lets the user provide their own context (and attachments), check what
will be submitted and the begin the builder conversation." Then: "Upload your own book or have ai generate would be good
as a first option." Then: "Make this only available to teachers".

Built as described in docs/storybook-builder.md. The calls made along the way:

- **Where**: the Story Library. Teachers get a "Make a book" button on `/library` and their newest books there;
  `/library/make` is the start (two cards, then Choices, Your words, Check). Students see books shared with their class
  under "From your teacher" and read them in the library reader. Registered before the library's own routes, so
  `/library/make` is never read as a book id.
- **Teachers only** (`storybook.canMake`: school staff and the platform admin), checked by one middleware on every page
  and API; everyone else gets the normal 404 (signed out: sign in). Not behind the Teacher plan: every teacher may make
  books, the plan only raises the daily number of Oomba turns (10 without, 60 with; `STORYBOOK_FREE_PER_DAY`,
  `STORYBOOK_PLAN_PER_DAY`), in the database like Mistake Hunt's free cap so it can't be reset or raced.
- **One chat engine**: the book's conversation is a surface of `services/oomba-chat.js` (jobs, progress card, Try again,
  Undo), shown with the shared panel. The site-wide companion is turned off on the book maker's pages (`companion:
  false`) so two Oomba panels never compete for the same side of the screen (the same reason as the Figures and
  Manipulatives pages before they folded in). Folding the book maker into the companion later is possible: its workflow
  (`writeBook`, `applyBook`, `undoChange`) is separate from the surface.
- **Screening and privacy**: everything the teacher typed or added is scrubbed (students' names, emails, phone numbers,
  links), the Builder's pre-filter reads all of it and the Builder's full input screening reads the teacher's own words
  and the story's opening, before the check step shows it and again on Start. Pictures the teacher adds are never sent
  to the book AI (only to the existing picture check, which refuses any person). The AI's book passes the Story
  Builder's word rules and classifier before a teacher sees it; words that fail twice end the turn with nothing saved.
- **Illustrations without an image model**: the AI picks scenes from the 2D art packs and the app draws them (SVG), the
  same characters on every page; a teacher may upload their own picture per page. The drawing sits behind a small
  illustrator interface so an image model can be added later (the owner's decision: cost and a new data flow).
- **Reading progress** has its own table (`made_book_reads`: page, trail, endings) rather than `story_reads`, whose
  rows are the manifest's books with question marks; it behaves the same way (the book opens where the reader stopped).
  Sharing is a class list, not a gradebook lesson; assigning with a due date and results like the library's books is a
  possible next step.
- **Open for the owner**: (1) the privacy page lists teacher AI tools one by one; the book maker sends the same kinds
  of data to the same processor, so it was not changed, but the owner may want a line for it (that would bump
  `LEGAL_UPDATED` and go in docs/legal-review.md). (2) Whether to add an image model. (3) Whether shared books should
  become gradebook assignments.
- Tests: `tests/unit/storybook.test.js` (12: access on every route for students, kids, grown-ups and signed-out
  visitors; the core rules; the first draft's prompt and drawn pictures; one retry with listed problems and repair;
  kid safety (word rules, classifier, students' names); merge, Undo and stale saves; scrubbing and screening before
  anything is sent; the cap (database, concurrency, nothing at the cap); the reader's choices, Back, The End, Start over
  and remembered place; print numbering and "turn to page N"; teacher pictures; class, school and account deletes).

## Book pictures: Google's Gemini image model (23 Nov 2026)

The owner: "The book maker should be deployed with an actual image generator that has a kids book drawing skill." Then:
"Moving forward with Google".

Built as described in docs/storybook-builder.md "Pictures". The calls made along the way:

- **Which model**: Gemini 3.1 Flash Image ("Nano Banana 2") on the Gemini API, model id `gemini-3.1-flash-image` (the
  generally available id; `STORYBOOK_IMAGE_MODEL` changes it), called over REST with the key in the `x-goog-api-key`
  header. It takes reference pictures in the same request, which is what keeps a book's characters the same on every
  page. About $0.067 a picture at 1K (Google's price list: 1,120 output tokens at $60 per million).
- **The drawing skill is ours**, not a hosted "style" product: one fixed picture-book house style in the prompt, a style
  seed per book, the safety rules in every prompt (no text in pictures, no real people, no brand characters, nothing
  scary), no living artist or book series named. Character sheets are drawn first from the look Oomba wrote for each
  character and sent with every page that shows them.
- **Safety is the same as for teachers' uploads**: only the picture prompts (book words that already passed the word
  rules, scrubbed of students' names again) and the book's own sheets go to Google; every picture that comes back passes
  the companion's picture check before it is kept or shown; Google's safety settings are at their strictest, and a
  block or a refusal falls back to the art-pack drawing with a calm note. The art packs stay as the fallback for no key,
  the budget resting and the daily limit.
- **Limits**: a daily picture count per teacher in the database (10 without the Teacher plan, 40 with; sheets and
  Redraws count), taken atomically at the moment of drawing, and every call through the AI budget (`recordImage`).
- **When pictures are drawn**: after each Oomba turn, only what is new or changed (a page's scene, characters, their
  looks or sheets); the teacher's own edits to the words never spend a picture. Redraw (with an optional note) is the
  teacher's way to ask again.
- **Privacy**: Google (the Gemini API) is a new processor for book pictures: a section on /privacy ("The book maker"),
  `LEGAL_UPDATED` 2026-11-23, and docs/legal-review.md "Book pictures". The owner sets `GEMINI_API_KEY` on Render; on
  the paid Gemini API, Google does not use prompts or pictures to improve its products (to confirm in the lawyer review).
- Tests: `tests/unit/storybook-pictures.test.js` (8, with a stand-in for Google: request shape, house style and seed,
  references, the key header, no student names; blocks and picture check refusals; the daily count under parallel
  requests; no key and the budget resting; Redraw and sheets; access; deleting).

## The book maker in the Oomba chat (23 Nov 2026)

The owner: "Make sure you can do this same process from the oomba chat." Then: "Clicking the make a book button should
just open up the chat and you should do the whole workflow there. The back and forth between the chat and the page is
confusing." Then: "Users should also be able to ask the oomba chat to make edits to a book they've made currently but
also in the past". And: "Choose your own adventure should also be able to be illustrated."

Built as described in docs/storybook-builder.md "In the Oomba chat". The calls made along the way:

- **One chat, the companion's.** For a teacher with the companion, Make a book opens the companion with the book
  maker's first card, the whole workflow is cards in that chat, and the book editor is a companion page (`book`): the
  editor's own Oomba panel is gone for them, so there is never a second chat. Every AI change to a book, from its page
  or any other, is a companion turn that runs the book maker's own functions (`writeBook`, `applyBook`, `undoChange`,
  `redraw`). An earlier draft of this design routed requests to the editor's own panel; the owner's second message
  replaced it. A book's earlier conversation in its own panel (made before this change) is kept in the database but not
  shown to these teachers.
- **Teachers without the companion** (no Teacher plan) keep the page steps and the editor's own chat: the book maker is
  for every teacher, the companion is not. Open for the owner: whether they should get the chat flow too.
- **Same service, no copied logic.** The cards use the page's lists and words; the check calls `cleanSetup`,
  `setupProblems` and `screenSetup`; Make my book calls `addPic` and `createBook` (split from `startBook`, which the page
  still uses); the daily turn cap and the picture count are the page's. Cards are answered without the AI; only the
  teacher's first message (and later change requests) go to the chat's AI, which fills in `makeBook` with what they said.
- **Your words never reach the chat's AI.** While the card waits for them, typed words and attachments go into the book
  only. One exception, noted: a picture attached to the very first message is read by the chat's AI, as every companion
  picture is (after the no-people check), before the book flow starts.
- **Books made in the past** are found among the teacher's own books only (`findMyBooks`); several that fit give a
  choice card (title, kind, date), none gives Make a book. Each change costs one of the day's turns wherever it is asked.
- **Pictures for every kind.** The normal kind is now "Picture book", and both kinds say every page (and every path) is
  illustrated. A Pictures choice (Oomba paints them, I'll add my own, No pictures) is on the page and in the chat, kept
  with the book; only the first ever paints or spends. The story map shows each page's picture.
- **Teachers only on the server**: the book tools are offered only to `storybook.canMake` accounts and refused by the
  tool runner, every card tap and every route for anyone else (a family grown-up tester with the companion included).
- Tests: `tests/unit/companion-book.test.js` (7), `tests/unit/companion-book-browser.test.js` (3, laptop and a 390 px
  phone), two more in `tests/unit/storybook-pictures.test.js` (an adventure painted on every page and ending, shown by
  the reader and the print copy; the Pictures choice).

## Book maker: my books as cards, with create, read, update and delete (23 Nov 2026)

The owner, with a phone screenshot of /library/make showing a plain list ("Milo and Zig Take Over the World · Picture
book · 7 pages · just now", the same book twice, and "Untitled book · Picture book · 0 pages · 30 minutes ago"): "you
should be able to perform crud on these books, and where My Books is shown in the library make sure they show up as
cards like the rest of the books".

- **The library's own card.** A teacher's books on /library (the newest 8) and /library/make are the Story Library's
  `lb-card` (cover, grade chip, title, meta line, actions) in the same `lb-grid`, so they look and wrap like every other
  book, two to a row on a phone. The cover is the first page's picture as the reader shows it (painted, the teacher's
  own, or the art-pack drawing), a calm placeholder when there is none. Chips: the grade and the kind. Meta: pages, when
  it changed, the classes it is shared with. (The old list's styles were in storybook.css, which /library never loaded:
  that is why it showed as plain text.)
- **Calm actions.** Read (as students see it) and Open (the editor) on the card; the less-used ones (Rename, Share with
  classes, Duplicate, Delete) in a small More menu (⋯) over the cover. The book page has its own More menu: Paint
  pictures again, Duplicate, Delete. Rename is in place (the title becomes a box). Delete asks in the site's own dialog,
  then the card goes with an Undo message for six seconds; the book is deleted when the message ends or the page is left
  (so Undo needs nothing on the server). Duplicate copies the pages, cast and every picture (nothing painted or counted
  again), adds "(copy)", is never shared, and spends no turn (no AI). There is no per-teacher book limit to respect; the
  route is rate-limited.
- **In the Oomba chat** (teachers only, own books only, on the server): `renameBook`, `duplicateBook`, `deleteBook` and
  `repaintBook` find the book as `changeBook` does (findMyBooks' matching, a choice card when several fit). They call the
  same functions as the cards. `deleteBook` never deletes: it shows a Delete / Keep card, and only Delete runs the
  delete.
- **The "Untitled book · 0 pages" row.** The book row is made when the teacher starts (createBook: the setup, the claimed
  pictures, one turn), and the first draft is a separate chat job keyed by the book. When that job failed (the AI
  resting or timing out, an answer that could not be read, which the 23 Nov fix to the writer's JSON reading addressed,
  a restart, or the turn not stored because the chat was busy), the empty row stayed and was listed as a normal book. Kept
  the row (the draft's job and its pictures are keyed by it) but it is never shown as a book: "Oomba is writing it"
  while its turn is live, otherwise "Didn't finish" with Try again (one turn, the first draft again) and Delete. Empty
  books older than an hour that are not being written are removed with everything under them: a minute after start-up,
  every hour, and whenever a teacher's books are listed.
- **Paint pictures again** (the book page and the chat, "redraw all the pictures in my Kip book"): after Google
  rejected the picture requests (fixed in #550 and #551), the owner's recent books fell back to the art pack. Every
  character sheet and page that shows an art-pack fallback (or was never queued) goes back in the same picture queue,
  at most as many as are left today (sheets first; the rest the next time), each counted when drawn, through the AI
  budget. Painted pictures are left alone.
- Tests: `tests/unit/storybook-books.test.js` (5), `tests/unit/companion-book-crud.test.js` (3), `tests/unit/storybook-books-browser.test.js` (3: laptop and a 390 px phone; `MY_BOOKS_SHOTS=<dir>` saves the pictures).

## Book pictures: a painting placeholder, never the art pack while painting (24 Nov 2026)

The owner: "Just tried the book generator again and it still used the same graphic pack". The production log for that
book (Render, 24 Nov 04:46 UTC) showed the opposite: the teacher opened the book page at 04:46:03, Google painted both
character sheets (04:46:06, 04:46:14) and all 6 pages (04:46:24 to 04:46:46, `storybook picture drawn`, `refs:1`), and
the page fetched the painted pictures (`/library/made/<id>/pic/<picId>` 200). But the teacher deleted the book at
04:46:44, about 40 seconds in, before painting finished. Painting worked; what the teacher saw while it ran was the
art-pack drawing ("Oomba kit") in every picture's place, so the book looked made from the kit.

- **While a picture is queued or painting** (and has no earlier painted picture), nobody sees the art-pack drawing for
  it: a calm "Oomba is painting this picture" placeholder (a soft paper panel, a gentle shimmer that stops with reduced
  motion, a small brush icon) is shown instead in the editor's page picture, the page list, the story map, the book's
  card on /library and /library/make, the reader (a student of a class it was shared with too: sharing stays allowed)
  and the print copy. The chat's book cards show no page pictures, so there is nothing to change there.
- **A progress line** at the top of the editor: "Painting your pictures: 3 of 8 ready. You can keep editing." (no word
  about a kit), then "All pictures painted." for a few seconds, and the line hides. The editor's poll swaps in each
  painted picture as it arrives (page, list and map); the cards ask for themselves again every few seconds while
  painting ("Painting pictures" in the meta line; Read stays) and swap in the painted cover.
- **The art pack only as a real fallback** (Google refused, today's pictures used, no key, waited too long): its one-line
  reason under the picture, with Paint pictures again right there (and in the line: "1 picture couldn't be painted...").
- **Pictures left queued by a restart** used to wait for the next change of the book; with the placeholder they would
  wait for ever, so the queue is kicked again 5 seconds after start-up and every 5 minutes when anything waits.
- Tests: `tests/unit/storybook-painting.test.js` (5: the placeholder, the reader, print copy and card while painting,
  the fallback, the restart kick; in a browser the editor and the cards while painting, the swap-in and "All pictures
  painted.", a fallback with Paint pictures again; `PAINT_SHOTS=<dir>` saves the pictures).

## Book pictures: the story and the pictures are free of the art kit (24 Nov 2026)

The owner, about "Tomas and Coco Help Out" (a boy, Tomas, and his chameleon friend, Coco): "I am worried that the Oomba
kit is somehow being passed into the prompt sent to Gemini or something because it seems like the book also refer to
the Dino as coco too if you look at the last photo... and idk why there is a Dino involved at all really". In the chat
Oomba had said "Coco has no matching animal picture, so the cast uses a green-looking friend drawn as the closest art,
and the look describes her as a chameleon"; the painted pages showed Coco as an elderly woman in a robe and as a
dinosaur, while the words said she tugged a kite string with her tail.

The worry was right. What leaked, and where (before this change):

- The writer was told to pick every cast member's `art` from the kit and "an animal character the closest animal id"
  (`storybook-illustrator.js`), and the book's JSON shape listed only `{"name", "art"}` for the cast (`storybook.js`
  `systemPrompt`), so a character's `look` was often missing and a character the kit had no sprite for was bent to one.
- The picture drawer sent the kit sprite's name as the character's kind (`storybook-draw.js` `charOf`:
  `kind: cat.chars[c.art].name`, e.g. "Triceratops" or "Wizard") and the kit world's name as the page's "Where"
  (`setting: cat.worlds[p.pic.world].name`, e.g. "Dino Valley"); `storybook-gemini.js` `sheetPrompt` and `pagePrompt`
  fell back to "a friendly <kind>" whenever the look was empty. So Coco's sheet could be "a friendly Triceratops", her
  pages were set in "Dino Valley", and a later turn that picked another sprite painted her again as an old wizard.

What changed, when Oomba paints the pictures (`storybook.js paints`: "Oomba paints them" and the picture model there):

- **The writer**: every cast member has `what` (what it is, as the story has it) and a `look` that starts with it; every
  picture a `setting` (where, in the book's words) beside its `scene`. It is told never to change what a character is,
  or how they look, to fit any list; the kit's `art` and `world` are optional, only for the stand-in drawing when
  painting falls back, and never mentioned to the teacher. A missing `what`, a look that doesn't name it, or a picture
  with no setting is sent back once with the problems listed. The new words pass the same word rules and names check.
- **The prompts to Google** carry only the book's own words: name, what and look for characters (no kit fallback; no
  look: "a friendly <what>"), the page's own setting for "Where". The sheet says what the character is and to draw it as
  exactly that, never as another animal, person or creature. A test checks that no kit sprite or world name reaches any
  request when the book's words don't use it.
- **The reply to the teacher** never talks about the kit: the prompt says so, and a sentence that mentions ready-made
  art, a stand-in, a sprite or the closest match is left out.
- **An audit trail**: each picture's final prompt (students' names already taken out; no pictures) is kept on its
  `made_book_draws` row (migration 0113), and the book's owner can open "What Oomba asked for" under the picture.
- **Books painted before**: nothing is repainted by itself, so their characters keep their sheets. Chosen as the
  simplest sane option: a teacher-triggered **Paint all pictures again** (the book page's More menu, after a short
  question, and the chat's `repaintBook` with `all: true`) paints every sheet and page again from the book's own words,
  counted against the day's pictures like any other. An old book's characters gain `what` on the book's next change by
  Oomba (the check asks for it); a character whose words change is painted again then, as before.
- Tests: `tests/unit/storybook-free-cast.test.js` (9).

## Oomba chat history (2026-11-24)
- **The owner:** "We need to include a chat history that users can go back to instead of deleting this all together
  when you start a new chat."
- **New chat** (services/companion.js `reset`) keeps the conversation: its row moves from `ctx_key 'main'` to
  `'h:<its id>'`, with its files, so retention (`prune`: the school's days after it was last used) and the account
  delete work as before. A chat with nothing said in it is just deleted. No question before New chat any more (nothing
  is lost). Answers of a chat moved to the history count as seen (no "new answer" dot for it).
- **Chat history** (🕘 in the panel's header, public/js/companion.js): the past chats in the conversation's place, newest
  first, each with its first message (names as the teacher wrote them) and when it was last used. Opening one makes it
  the conversation again (the open one goes to the history); each has Delete (asked first). At most 50 are kept (the
  oldest go). Routes: `GET /api/companion/chats`, `POST /api/companion/chats/:id/open`, `POST .../delete`.
- **Files:** a file is only usable from the open conversation (`fileOf`); a past chat's files come back with it.
- **/privacy:** `info.privacy.companion.p5` says so (docs/legal-review.md "Oomba companion: chat history").

## Classroom focus: the Builder without the kit (24 Nov 2026)

The owner: "for classroom game and classroom lesson, I don't want it attached to the Oomba kit anymore. And so there
won't be any graphics per se, but this is all going to be like geared towards, like, of course we can still keep like
the category boards, the class survey, bingo, quiet games... I really want to move away from the Oomba kit and the
arcade element." And: "Classroom lessons suggestion is good", "Rebuild the quiz memory and word games as plain classroom
formats", "Yes students can still build lessons for themselves", "The games being built should be professional looking
but still fun engaging and interactive".

- **One switch, off by default**: `ARCADE` (`config.arcade`). Off, the Builder never offers or uses the Oomba Kit (the v1
  kit, Kit 2, the 2D art, Three.js worlds) for a new build. On, everything is as it was, byte for byte (the arcade
  `SYSTEM_PROMPT` and `TOOLS` keep their hashes). Nothing is deleted: the kit, the vendor files, the kit templates and every
  game made on them stay and keep playing.
- **Two fixed prefixes, one per mode**: `prompt.js` `SYSTEM_PROMPT_FOCUS` is the same body with the kit, Kit 2, 2D art and
  3D parts swapped for classroom ones (checked once when the module loads: each swap must match exactly once, and the result
  may not name the kit) and `CLASSROOM_RULES_FOCUS` in place of the CLASSROOM, KIT 2 (short), 2D ART (short) and KIT rules;
  `TOOLS_FOCUS` offers only the classroom starters to `start_from_template` (no world, hero, sprite or friends). Each is
  the same bytes for every classroom build, so it caches like the arcade one.
- **Per turn** (`claude.js`): with the arcade side off, no KIT 2, 2D ART, 3D or LIVE rules for a new game, whatever the
  words ask for. A game made on the kit before (`prompt.js legacyKit`) keeps its engine: its own rules (the KIT RULES, KIT 2,
  2D ART, 3D or LIVE) come as a block of their own on its own turns only. `start_from_template` refuses a kit template.
- **The plan** (`plan.js`): `planEngine` never returns `kit2`, `world3d` or `2d`; quiz, memory and word are the plain
  `classquiz`, `classmemory` and `classword` starters and skip the look, world and characters steps; any other arcade kind
  is made as the closest plain classroom game. `typeGroups` has one group, the classroom types. Classroom lessons stay on
  Oomba Canvas (not the kit).
- **Three new starters**, the classroom formats of quiz, memory and word: Class Quiz (multiple choice, an optional timer,
  a score, a review of every answer with a tick or a cross, "Try the missed ones"), Memory Match (term and meaning, or
  picture and word; solo or 2-4 teams taking turns; a 3D flip), Word Lab (a word list three ways: Unscramble from a clue,
  Spell it after hearing it, Fill the gap). Each: keyboard play, 375 px, an Edit box where the teacher pastes their own
  content (one item per line, kept on that device only), no kit tags.
- **One look for every classroom starter**: `templates/classroom-style.css` (the Oomba design system: Bricolage
  Grotesque, page #F4F1E6, cards #FFFDF2, Mint, Leaf, Ink, Spark, 20 px corners, calm motion that stops for reduced
  motion), put in at each starter's `<!--CLASSROOM_STYLE-->`. The font is self-hosted for frames at
  `/vendor/oomba-classroom/1.0.0/fonts/` (font-src only, `frame.js CLASSROOM_FONT_PATH`): no font service, so nothing
  about a student reaches another company. Sound is off until someone presses Sound.
- **Live**: Oomba Live needs the kit's live pack, and a plain live client is a bigger piece of work (the hosting check,
  the scanner and the frame all trust the pack today). So for now no classroom game is played live with the arcade side
  off: the setup step and the Studio say why (`buildSetup.play.why.plain`); a class plays on the board together, or each
  student opens it on their own device. Bingo already deals a card per device. A kit game made before can still be made live.
- **The Studio**: no "Make it an arcade game" switch and no worlds and heroes picker for a plain game; a new game can not
  start from a kit template (`/api/studio/new`).
- Tests: `tests/unit/builder-focus.test.js`; the kit tests set `config.arcade = true`.

## No public games: share with connections and classes (24 Nov 2026)
- **The owner:** "Furthermore, users should no longer be able to publish their games publically. You should only be able
  to share with your connections and classrooms."
- **Flag** `PUBLIC_GAMES` (`config.publicGames`, off by default; `services/games.js` `openToAll`). Off: `sharingOptions`
  never offers Everyone or My school (students, teachers, kids, grown-ups: "only with your connections and classrooms"),
  `publish()` refuses `public` (`code: 'noPublic'`) and `school` (`code: 'noSchool'`), the Studio's share sheet has
  neither choice and the school setting "allowed to go public" is hidden. The choices left: Only me, Friends (a grown-up's
  grown-up connections), My family (grown-ups) and My classes. Official games (seed-games/, by Oomba Academy) stay open
  to everyone.
- **Games that were public or shared with the school before** are not changed in the database. They are read as shared with their maker's
  connections and classes: accepted friends, a family link either way (the grown-up and their linked child), and the
  people in a live class with the maker (students and teachers). The maker and the platform admin always open them;
  anyone else (signed out included) gets the normal "not shared" page. `canView` and `visibleWhere` use the same rule, so
  they appear on no list for anyone else (Play, Learn, search, `/u/` profiles, "Games by players", which is gone while the
  flag is off); the sitemap and Oomba's game search were official-only already. Class rooms, pushes, assignments and
  lesson steps reach such a game only in a class its maker is in; a schoolmate outside the maker's classes no longer opens a
  'school' game. Its maker sees it as "Friends and classes" and can
  still Update it at that level (a clean version goes live at once, a flagged one waits for a person, like a class game).
  A request for Everyone or My school still waiting in the review queue is approved at the level the game is live at (else Friends).

  describe public publishing.
## Castle Clash: a chess-site UI, 4,000+ puzzles, progress and wood sounds (24 Nov 2026)
- **The owner:** "You mentioned a while back that there is an open source repo with a ton of puzzles for our Chess
  game. Can we add those puzzles to our chess game, remove the Oomba kit and make it look more like chess.com ui
  (obviously not copying). There should be a progress tracker for this and it should be fun and interactive. Make the
  chess pieces have actual chess piece sounds when sound is on."
- **No kit.** `seed-games/castle-clash.html` loads no kit script (no world, title, pause, icons, owl or animal busts).
  Its own UI: a DOM board (64 cells under piece elements that slide with CSS transforms), our own Staunton-style SVG
  pieces, three board themes (Meadow, Walnut, Ocean; a version 1 save's courtyard/candy become Meadow, wood Walnut, space
  Ocean), last-move, check and legal-move marks, drag and tap, player panels with captures and the material lead, a
  two-column move list, flip, undo, hint, draw, resign. Chrome in the Oomba tokens. The robot is **Oomba Bot** (a drawn
  robot face) at the same four levels; the kingdoms are now White and Black. The rules engine, the robot search, the
  lessons, the Beginner path (the 24 hand-made puzzles), the online match protocol (mv/act numbers) and the
  `window.__brbTest` hooks are kept.
- **Puzzles** come from the Lichess puzzle database (CC0): `scripts/chess-puzzles.mjs` streams the export (curl + Node's
  zstd; the file is pzstd's format, so the skippable frames are dropped), keeps Popularity >= 90, NbPlays >= 1000,
  RatingDeviation <= 80, rating 600 to 2199 and at most four moves to find, replays each one with the game's own engine
  (legal moves; mate puzzles end in mate; others do not lose material), spreads each 200-point band over 16 theme
  groups (520 per band, 4,160 in all, 435 KB) and writes eight packs plus their sha384 into the game. The frame CSP has no
  `connect-src` for /vendor, so the packs are scripts under `/vendor/data/castle-clash/` (like every other game's data
  packs), not JSON fetched from `/vendor/chess-puzzles/`. A checksum that happens to spell a word the content scanner
  blocks gets a salt line.
- **Rating.** Elo-like, starting at 800, K from 40 down to 16. A clean solve raises it; a mistake or the solution lowers
  it once; a solve after a hint leaves it alone (kinder than a loss, no free gain). Rated puzzles, theme packs and the
  first daily puzzle of the day count; Puzzle Rush (3 minutes, 3 mistakes, harder as you go) and the Beginner path do not.
- **Progress** (in `castle-clash-v1`, v 2, through the SDK storage shim): rating history, solved total, today, day
  streak, accuracy, best in a row, best rush, per-theme results, lesson and path stars, robot wins. The leaderboard stays
  robot points (`BRB.score.submit(points, 'robot wins')`): a puzzle rating goes down as well as up, so it is not a
  "best score".
- **Sounds.** No clean-licence recording set was reachable (Lichess's sets are AGPL or CC BY-NC-SA; chess.com's are not
  open), so the game synthesizes wooden knocks (a band-passed contact click plus the decaying modes of a piece and the
  board) and soft marimba notes with WebAudio into buffers at first use. They play only while `BRB.sfx.muted` is false
  (the site's sound switch, also the game's speaker button). No files, so nothing under `/vendor/chess-sounds/`.
- Tests: `tests/unit/castle-clash.test.js` (10), `tests/e2e/castle-clash.spec.js`.
